## AgentAction

AgentAction (type, sygnal)
One entry of `agent.actions`, typed by the model's data type D for that action: no data (undefined, void, null, or the DOM event a click delivers): no `input`; an untyped component: `input` optional; otherwise `input` is required and its schema's output must be assignable to D.
type AgentAction<STATE, D>
Members:
  description: string - What the action does, for the model (WebMCP: at most 500 characters)
  consequential?: boolean - Ask the user before running it (the chat behavior's `pending`, WebMCP's confirm)
  when?: (state: STATE, bag: ReadBag$1<STATE>) => boolean - Offered only while this is true (cached by state, props and context identity; the instance's view bag last)
  idempotent?: boolean - A call that changes nothing is a success (`{ ok: true, unchanged: true }`), not an error
  until?: string | ((state: STATE, bag: ReadBag$1<STATE>) => boolean) - The call answers once the action's result is in state, not right after the action: the name of one of the com…
  timeout?: number - With `until`: answer `{ ok: true, pending: true }` after this many ms (default 10,000)
  input?: AgentSchema<any> | AgentSchema<D>

AgentAction.consequential?: boolean
Ask the user before running it (the chat behavior's `pending`, WebMCP's confirm)

AgentAction.idempotent?: boolean
A call that changes nothing is a success (`{ ok: true, unchanged: true }`), not an error

AgentAction.timeout?: number
With `until`: answer `{ ok: true, pending: true }` after this many ms (default 10,000)
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/http.md

## AgentAction.until

AgentAction.until?: string | ((state: STATE, bag: ReadBag$1<STATE>) => boolean)
The call answers once the action's result is in state, not right after the action: the name of one of the component's `resources` (done when it is neither loading nor refreshing), or a function of the state (for a result a reply action writes; the action's own reducer should mark it pending). Checked after the action and after every render that changed something
Example: until: 'search'
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/ai.md

## AgentDeclaration

AgentDeclaration (type, sygnal)
The `agent` static: what agents may do with a component and see of it. Only the listed actions are exposed, as tools `<name>_<action>` (snake case) plus `<name>_read`; a Collection item component's actions are one tool per action with an `id` parameter (`item` when the input has its own `id`).
type AgentDeclaration<STATE = any, ACTIONS = any>
Members:
  name: string - Tool name prefix: `todos` -> todos_add, todos_read (letters, digits, _)
  description?: string
  read?: (state: STATE, bag: ReadBag$1<STATE>) => unknown - What the model sees of this component: in its context after every flush, and in call results (7.2: the instan…
  label?: (state: STATE) => string - A Collection item's label for the model.
  untrusted?: boolean - `read` (and `label`) return user-entered strings (WebMCP's untrustedContentHint;
  actions?: keyof ACTIONS extends never ? { [action: string]: AgentAction<S…
  queries?: { [query: string]: AgentQuery<STATE>; } - Read-only tools that take an input: `{ find: { description, input, run: (state, input) => result } }`

## AgentDeclaration.label

AgentDeclaration.label?: (state: STATE) => string
A Collection item's label for the model. User text unless `untrusted: false`: then the key parameter lists ids only and the labels go with the data (the chat behavior's app state as `<name>_labels`, the command bar's decision `state.labels`)
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/ui.md

## AgentDeclaration.name

AgentDeclaration.name: string
Tool name prefix: `todos` -> todos_add, todos_read (letters, digits, _)
Example: name="due"
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/testing.md

## AgentDeclaration.queries

AgentDeclaration.queries?: { [query: string]: AgentQuery<STATE>; }
Read-only tools that take an input: `{ find: { description, input, run: (state, input) => result } }`

## AgentDeclaration.read

AgentDeclaration.read?: (state: STATE, bag: ReadBag$1<STATE>) => unknown
What the model sees of this component: in its context after every flush, and in call results (7.2: the instance's view bag last, `{ ...props, state, context, uid }`)
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/ai.md

## AgentDeclaration.untrusted

AgentDeclaration.untrusted?: boolean
`read` (and `label`) return user-entered strings (WebMCP's untrustedContentHint; the chat behavior names the declaration as untrusted in its app-state block); `false`: only the app's own text. Unset, it is inferred (WebMCP: SYG244): any string is user text except values under keys named `id`, `status`, `type` or `kind`, and values that are one of this declaration's input enum values
Example: untrusted: true
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/ai.md

Without a JSON Schema form the tool isn't offered (SYG240).

## Animate

Animate (type, sygnal/three)
Per-frame values: `animate={{ rotation: (t, dt, object) => [0, t, 0] }}` on a scene element. The target calls each function every frame (seconds since the page started, and since the last frame) and writes the result to the object, outside state, views and the DOM patch.
export type Animate = Record<string, (t: number, dt: number, object: any) => unknown>

## ApiStream.resume

ApiStream.resume?: string | true
resume after a reconnect the driver makes (EventSource gave up: a proxy 502, a non-2xx on the `headers` path) from the last event id. Over fetch (`headers`) it is sent as `Last-Event-ID`; the native EventSource can't send it, so it goes on the URL: `?lastEventId=<id>` (`true`) or `?<name>=<id>` (a parameter name). EventSource's own retries send `Last-Event-ID` anyway
Example: resume: true | 'param'

## ApiStream.staleAfterMs

ApiStream.staleAfterMs?: number
a connection that stays silent this long (ms) is taken as dead (a half-open socket behind a proxy): it is closed as a drop, `close` gets `{ stale: true, willReconnect }`, and the reconnect policy applies. Every event counts; over fetch (an `sse` with `headers`) any bytes do, heartbeat comments (`: ping`) included, while the native EventSource needs a real event (a `message`, or a named event listed in `events`). Set it above the server's heartbeat interval
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/sockets.md

## AppErrorPhase

AppErrorPhase (type, sygnal)

## CheckPluginOptions.include

Files, directories or globs to check, relative to the Vite root. By default the existing ones of src/, pages/ and renderer/ (Vike apps), else the project root (node_modules, dist and other build output are skipped); a one-time notice is logged when the default finds no directory or when none of the given paths exists.
Read: node_modules/sygnal/dist/guide/http.md

## CheckPluginOptions.overlay

CheckPluginOptions.overlay?: false | "error" | "warn"
Error-severity findings also open Vite's error overlay ('error'); false: never. Every finding is printed in the terminal and logged in the browser console (sygnal-check's codes are currently all warnings or info, so in practice that is where they go). Warnings never use the overlay, because Vite's client reloads the page on the next HMR update while an overlay is open: 'warn' is still accepted, and treated as 'error' with a one-time notice. The overlay is sent only to the page that loads (not to every client), closed before each HMR update and sent again after the re-check.
Read: node_modules/sygnal/dist/guide/ai-compose.md

## Comp.route

Comp.route?: string | ((state: SpecOf<T, "state", any> & SpecOf<T, "calculated", {}>, bag: DeclarationBag<SpecOf<T, "state", any> & SpecOf<T, "calculated", {}>, SpecOf<T, "props", { [prop: string]: any; }>, SpecOf<T, "context", {}>>) => string | false)
The router's reply action (`makeRouter()`): `App.route = 'ROUTE'`. The driver sends this instance ROUTE with the `Route` (`{ name, params, query, hash, path }`) once declared and on every change; the reducer stores it (`ROUTE: (state, route) => ({ ...state, route })`). The first (outermost) declarer gets each route first and may redirect from that entry (`ROUTER: { to: 'login', replace: true }`); the others get it right after its ROUTE ran, only if no redirect happened. All in one flush: every declarer has its first route before the first render is patched, and a navigation is one patch; past 32 navigations in a row (a redirect loop) each next one waits a task.
Example: App.initialState = { route: router.current(), user: null }

## ComposeOptions.busy

ComposeOptions.busy?: "abort" | "queue"
what a COMPOSE does while a composition is in flight: 'abort' (default) starts it at once (the step in flight is aborted); 'queue' keeps one in flight: the COMPOSE waits in `queued` (a newer one replaces it) and starts when the one in flight ends, which still lands first (DONE runs; the waiting one starts on the layout DONE's entries left). ## DEFAULT_LIMITS

DEFAULT_LIMITS (const, sygnal/sandbox)
DEFAULT_LIMITS: Readonly<SandboxLimits>
Members:
  memoryBytes: number - QuickJS's heap (default 32 MB)
  stackBytes: number - QuickJS's stack (default 256 KB; at most 384 KB: above that a recursion can crash the WASM module)
  maxWasmBytes: number - the instance's whole linear memory, ArrayBuffers included (default 64 MB)
  bootMs: number - kernel + component + first render (default 1000 ms)
  callMs: number - one event, timer or fetch reply with its render (default 100 ms; polled, see the guide)
  cpuShare: number - guest time per rolling second (default 0.5)
  hardMs: number - worker: terminated when it doesn't answer the watchdog this long (default 1000 ms)
  maxTimers: number - pending timers (default 64)
  minTimerMs: number - the shortest timer (default 4 ms)
  maxFetches: number - fetches in flight (default 4)
  maxMessageBytes: number - one render or response (default 1 MB)
  maxLogs: number - console lines (default 100)

Each entry derives a request from state and (7.2, as every declaration static) the bag, the view's `{ ...props, state, context, uid }`: `(state, { id, context: { route } }) => '/api/items/' + (id ?? route.params.id)`; re-run when the state, the context or a prop changes; falsy means idle: `Quote.resources = { quote: (state) => state.id && '/api/quotes/' + state.id }`. `state.quote` is a `Resource`: `{ status: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error', data, error, refreshing }`, written by the built-in RESOURCE action (idle until the first request).

## DefineComponentOptions.route

DefineComponentOptions.route?: string | ((state: STATE & CALCULATED, bag: DeclarationBag<STATE & CALCULATED, PROPS, CONTEXT>) => string | false)
The router's reply action (`makeRouter()`): `App.route = 'ROUTE'`. The driver sends this instance ROUTE with the `Route` (`{ name, params, query, hash, path }`) once declared and on every change; the reducer stores it (`ROUTE: (state, route) => ({ ...state, route })`). The first (outermost) declarer gets each route first and may redirect from that entry (`ROUTER: { to: 'login', replace: true }`); the others get it right after its ROUTE ran, only if no redirect happened. All in one flush: every declarer has its first route before the first render is patched, and a navigation is one patch; past 32 navigations in a row (a redirect loop) each next one waits a task.

## FetchProgress

## FetchRequest.abort

FetchRequest.abort: string | true
Cancel. Reply actions: `{ abort: 'LOADED' }` aborts this instance's requests in flight whose key (`key`, else `ok`, else `error`) is 'LOADED'; `{ abort: true, key: 'search' }` does the same by key. Without reply actions: `{ category: 'search', abort: true }` aborts this component's requests in that category (all of them, reply-action ones included, without a category or key). Nothing is delivered for a cancelled request.
Example: { abort: 'RESULTS' }

## FetchRequest.stream

read a 2xx body as a stream of pieces as they arrive (a POST that streams: a copilot endpoint answering `data: {...}` lines). 'sse': each event's `data`, JSON-parsed when it parses; 'ndjson': each non-blank line, JSON-parsed; 'text': the text as it arrives. Each piece is the `chunk` action (else a reply on `select(category)`); the end of the body (or the `done` piece) is the `ok` action, with `{ status, headers }` (FetchStreamEnd). `latest`, `abort`, `key` and `timeoutMs` (here: the time to the first byte) apply; `retry`, `cache`, `parse`, `validate` and `progress` don't. interface FormState<V = any>
Members:
  values: V
  initial: V - The values the form started with (or was last saved / reset with)
  errors: FieldErrors - Every current schema error by field name, shown or not
  touched: Record<string, boolean>
  server: FieldErrors - Server errors (`form.ERRORS`)
  remote: FieldErrors - Async check results by field name ('' = passed)
  pending: Record<string, any> - Field name → the value its check is running for
  submitting: boolean - A valid submit sent its request (the submit entry has the `http` sink) and has no `form.DONE` / `form.ERRORS`…
  submitted: boolean - `form.DONE` arrived, or a submit that sends nothing was dispatched
  submitCount: number
  queued: boolean - A submit waits for an async check or an async schema
  validating: boolean - The schema hasn't answered for the current values yet (an async one is running; also at the start)
  validated: boolean - The schema has answered at least once since the start (or the last `form.RESET`)
  progress: { phase: 'upload' | 'download'; loaded: number; total: number |… - the submit request's last progress step, when it is sent with `progress: 'form.PROGRESS'`;
  resets: number - how many times the form started over (`form.RESET`, `resetOnShow`).
  added: Record<string, any> - the dynamic fields on the form now (the `dynamic` option's entries for the host's state): path → start value.
  kept: Record<string, true> - the dynamic fields that went while their values stay in `values` (`keepRemoved`, the default): path → true.

## GENERATED_LIMITS

GENERATED_LIMITS (const, sygnal/sandbox)
A generated part's limits: heap 16 MB, instance 48 MB, stack 256 KB, boot 500 ms, 50 ms per event, worker watchdog 1 s

Members:
  memoryBytes?: number - QuickJS's heap (default 32 MB)
  stackBytes?: number - QuickJS's stack (default 256 KB; at most 384 KB: above that a recursion can crash the WASM module)
  maxWasmBytes?: number - the instance's whole linear memory, ArrayBuffers included (default 64 MB)
  bootMs?: number - kernel + component + first render (default 1000 ms)
  callMs?: number - one event, timer or fetch reply with its render (default 100 ms; polled, see the guide)
  cpuShare?: number - guest time per rolling second (default 0.5)
  hardMs?: number - worker: terminated when it doesn't answer the watchdog this long (default 1000 ms)
  maxTimers?: number - pending timers (default 64)
  minTimerMs?: number - the shortest timer (default 4 ms)
  maxFetches?: number - fetches in flight (default 4)
  maxMessageBytes?: number - one render or response (default 1 MB)
  maxLogs?: number - console lines (default 100)
Read: node_modules/sygnal/dist/guide/ai-compose.md

## HTTP

HTTP (driver sink and source, from makeFetchDriver)
An HTTP driver over `fetch`: `run(App, { HTTP: makeFetchDriver() })`. Canonical: a request with reply actions (`HTTP: (state) => ({ url: '/api/quote', ok: 'LOADED', error: 'FAILED' })`) whose outcome arrives as the LOADED (parsed body) or FAILED (FetchFailure) action of the sending instance.
Request (FetchRequest):
  url: string - Request URL (prefixed with the driver's `baseUrl`)
  ok?: string - Reply action that receives the parsed body of a 2xx response (the Response with `parse: 'response'`;
  error?: string - Reply action that receives a failure, `{ error, status?, body?, headers?, request }` (FetchFailure)
  key?: string - Reply actions: the `latest` / `abort` group (default: the `ok` action, else `error`, else `chunk`).
  category?: string - Without reply actions: tag read back with `select(category)` / `errors(category)`;
  method?: string - Default: 'POST' when `json` or `body` is set, else 'GET'
  headers?: Record<string, string> | Headers - Merged over the driver's `headers`, case-insensitively (names are sent lowercased)
  query?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | (string | number | b… - Appended as a query string (`{ q: 'dune' }` → `?q=dune`), before any `#fragment`;
  json?: any - Sent as JSON.stringify(json), with `Content-Type: application/json` unless set
  multipart?: Record<string, MultipartValue | readonly MultipartValue[]> - a multipart/form-data body, written as data: `{ file: state.file, title: state.title }`.
  body?: any - Raw body (string, FormData, Blob, ...)
  progress?: string | true - report upload and download progress. An action name: each step arrives as that action of the sending instance…
  …
Example: HTTP: makeFetchDriver()
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/http.md

## InspectAction.trigger

InspectAction.trigger: InspectActionTrigger
'intent': returned by the component's intent. 'builtin': BOOTSTRAP, INITIALIZE, DISPOSE or READY. 'reply': named as a reply action by a request (`ok: 'NAME'` / `error: 'NAME'`) or a `connections` entry (statically: a string literal; at runtime: a request the instance was seen sending). 'next': dispatched with next() (statically: a next('NAME') literal; at runtime: a model-only action whose STATE reducer was seen running). 'unknown': none of these is known.

## LazyComponent.route

LazyComponent.route?: string | ((state: any, bag: DeclarationBag<any, PROPS, {}>) => string | false)
The router's reply action (`makeRouter()`): `App.route = 'ROUTE'`. The driver sends this instance ROUTE with the `Route` (`{ name, params, query, hash, path }`) once declared and on every change; the reducer stores it (`ROUTE: (state, route) => ({ ...state, route })`). The first (outermost) declarer gets each route first and may redirect from that entry (`ROUTER: { to: 'login', replace: true }`); the others get it right after its ROUTE ran, only if no redirect happened. All in one flush: every declarer has its first route before the first render is patched, and a navigation is one patch; past 32 navigations in a row (a redirect loop) each next one waits a task.
Example: App.initialState = { route: router.current(), user: null }

## RecordOptions.redact

Default true. `true` or `{ keep, also }`: the strings of typed input (intent actions dispatched while a text-entry DOM event was delivered, and later actions of those types), server replies, setState values and the types in `also` are pseudonymized (same shape, equal strings stay equal); never the types in `keep`, nor next() data. Checkpoints are masked. A redacted string the model branches on makes the replay diverge there: add it to `keep`. `false`: nothing redacted.

## RenderOptions.autoConnect

RenderOptions.autoConnect?: boolean
Fake socket connections open by themselves (default true; reconnects too; a t.push / t.drop right after the declaration opens it first). false: they stay 'connecting' until t.open(), for "Connecting…" assertions and failures to open (t.drop on a connecting one).
Example: renderComponent(C, { autoConnect: false })
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/testing.md

## RenderOptions.autoDispose

RenderOptions.autoDispose?: boolean
Under Vitest, a handle created inside a test (or its beforeEach) is disposed when that test finishes, passed or failed (`onTestFinished`, as Testing Library's auto-cleanup). `false` keeps it alive until `t.dispose()`. Default true. Other runners: `afterEach(cleanup)`.

## RenderOptions.router

RenderOptions.router?: Router<any>
The app's router (the object `makeRouter()` returns). With no driver for `routerSink` in `drivers`, renderComponent runs its real driver over an in-memory window (location, history, popstate a task later, document listeners): read with `t.location`, drive with `t.navigate` / `t.back` / `t.forward`; the commands the app sent are `t.sent('ROUTER')`. Required when the component declares `route` (renderComponent throws naming it otherwise). The real `window.location` is never changed.
Example: export const router = makeRouter({ routes: { home: '/', task: '/tasks/:id', admin: '/admin', notFound: '*' } })  // first match wins
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/router.md

A driverless sink that gets `{ connections }` / `{ to }` values (e.g. `WS` with no `drivers: { WS }`) is a fake makeSocketDriver: diffed per component and connection name, `open`/`message`/`close`/`error` as reply actions of the sender (no `close` for closes the app makes), other events on `WS.select(name)`, shared by URL, reconnect per the spec on the test's timers (fake timers included). ## RenderResult.fail

RenderResult.fail: (sinkName: string, error: any, target?: string | FakeReplyOptions | Record<string, any> | ((request: any) => boolean)) => Promise<void>
Fail a pending request (chosen as in respond): one with reply actions (`error: 'FAILED'`) gets `{ error, request, status?, body? }` as its `FAILED` action, on its sender; a plain one `{ error, category, request, status, body }` on `HTTP.errors(category)`. `error`: an HTTP status (an error response: 404 → the driver's Error 'HTTP 404: url', status 404), or an Error / message (a network failure: no status). On the LLM fake: the stream fails with `error` (a number: Error 'HTTP 429' with `status`), and the request's `error` action gets `{ key, error, request }`; a request with no `error` action throws (the driver would only log it, SYG678).

## RootComp.route

RootComp.route?: string | ((state: SpecOf<T, "state", any> & SpecOf<T, "calculated", {}>, bag: DeclarationBag<SpecOf<T, "state", any> & SpecOf<T, "calculated", {}>, {}, SpecOf<T, "context", {}>>) => string | false)
The router's reply action (`makeRouter()`): `App.route = 'ROUTE'`. The driver sends this instance ROUTE with the `Route` (`{ name, params, query, hash, path }`) once declared and on every change; the reducer stores it (`ROUTE: (state, route) => ({ ...state, route })`). The first (outermost) declarer gets each route first and may redirect from that entry (`ROUTER: { to: 'login', replace: true }`); the others get it right after its ROUTE ran, only if no redirect happened. ## SYG101

SYG101 (warn): Intent action has no model entry
The intent returns an action stream whose name has no matching key in `model`. Events on that stream are produced but nothing handles them, so the action silently does nothing. Built-in actions (`BOOTSTRAP`, `INITIALIZE`, `DISPOSE`, `READY`, and `RESOURCE`, which the core writes for a `resources` static) and internal `__*` actions are never reported. `HYDRATE` is not built in since 6.0: it is an ordinary action name.
Fix: Add a model entry with the same name, e.g. `model = { SAVE: (state) => ({ ...state, saved: true }) }`, or remove or rename the intent action so it matches an existing model key.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG101

## SYG102

SYG102 (info): Model entry is unreachable
A model entry has no intent action of the same name and is not a built-in action (`BOOTSTRAP`, `INITIALIZE`, `DISPOSE`, `READY`, `RESOURCE`; `HYDRATE` is an ordinary action since 6.0), so nothing in the intent can trigger it. A request also triggers the reply actions it names (`{ url, ok: 'LOADED', error: 'FAILED' }` sent to a driver sink, and an HTTP request's `progress: 'UPLOAD_PROGRESS'`), and so does a `connections` entry (`message`, `open`, `close`, `error`) or a request a `resources` entry derives (`ok`, `error`). A `RESOURCE` entry replaces the built-in reducer that writes `state[name]` for a `resources` static.
Fix: Add the action to the component's `intent`, name it in a request (`HTTP: (state) => ({ url, ok: 'ACTION' })`), dispatch it with `next('ACTION')` from another entry, or remove the dead model entry.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG102

## SYG103

SYG103 (info): Intent selector matched no rendered element
A selector passed to `DOM.select()` in the intent has not matched any element the component rendered, so its events never fire (often a typo in the class or id). The dev entry skips selectors whose class/id/tag tokens all appear in the view source (assumed conditionally rendered); others are reported as info on the first check and escalated to warn after at least 3 renders and about 2 s of render-idle time with no match. Under `renderComponent`, `simulateEvent()` on a selector that matches no rendered element throws an error instead; with `{ allowMissing: true }` the event is dropped and SYG103 is reported.
Fix: Check the selector against the `className`/`id` in the view. If the element is rendered by a child component, handle the event inside that child instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG103

## SYG104

SYG104 (warn): Intent selector crosses an isolation boundary
An intent selector matches nothing in the component's own scope, but does match elements rendered inside a child component or Collection item. Child components are isolated, so the parent's `DOM` source never receives events from those elements and the action never fires. The dev entry checks the real DOM after renders, `renderComponent` checks the mock vtree, and `sygnal-check` finds the class/id, or the control (`DOM.click(Remove)` with `<Remove>` rendered by the child), only in a child component's view.
Fix: Handle the event inside the child component and send it up with `PARENT` (read it in the parent with `CHILD.select(Child)`), or broadcast it with `EVENTS`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG104

## SYG105

SYG105 (info): EVENTS type selected but never emitted, or emitted but never selected
An `EVENTS` bus type is emitted with nothing selecting it, or selected with `EVENTS.select(type)` but never emitted. The bus is a broadcast, so an event that nobody has subscribed to when it is emitted is dropped; a mismatched name usually means a typo. At runtime the emitted-not-selected case is reported when the event is emitted, while selected-not-emitted is only reported on demand via `checkEventBus()` (inspect/test helpers); `EVENTS.select()` with no type counts as selecting everything. The static checker compares string-literal types across the scanned files and reports warn, or info when non-literal emits/selects exist.
Fix: Make the names match: emit from a model entry, e.g. `{ EVENTS: event('TYPE', data) }`, and subscribe with `EVENTS.select('TYPE')` in the receiving component's intent.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG105

## SYG106

SYG106 (warn): Parent prop is overwritten by a reserved view argument
The view is called with `{ ...props, state, children, slots, context, uid }`, so a prop named `children`, `slots`, `context` or `uid` passed by the parent is overwritten and never reaches the child. A `state` prop is also reported when its value is not a state lens (a field-name string or a `{ get, set }` object), because Sygnal reads `state` as the child's state lens rather than as data. Reported once per component and prop, as a warning, or as an error in strict mode (`--strict` has no static SYG106 rule;
Fix: Rename the prop in both parent and child (e.g. `contextValue`, `itemId` instead of `uid`, or `item` instead of `state`); to give the child a slice of parent state use `state="fieldName"`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG106

## SYG107

SYG107 (warn): DOM property name in the wrong case
Sygnal sets a JSX name on an HTML element as the DOM property of that name, in that case (React keeps a table of attribute names; Preact falls back to an attribute). A name the element has no property for creates an unused JavaScript property on the element: nothing is rendered, nothing fails, and the server-rendered markup and the mock DOM of `renderComponent` still show it. The usual cause is the case.
Fix: Write the DOM property's name: `<input autocomplete="off" inputMode="numeric" maxLength={4} />`, `<img srcset={…} />`, `<td colSpan={2} />`. For an attribute that has no DOM property, use the attrs module: `attrs-autocomplete="off"` or `attrs={{ autocomplete: 'off' }}`. `sygnal-check --fix` renames the attribute.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG107

## SYG108

SYG108 (error): Intent selector is not valid CSS
An intent selector (`DOM.click('.x')`, `DOM.select('.x')`) that the browser can't parse. Sygnal matches selectors with `Element.matches()`, so an invalid one throws a `SyntaxError` on every matching event, and the throw takes the component's other DOM listeners down with it. The usual cause is a utility-class name used as the hook: a Tailwind class like `hover:bg-red-500` (the `:bg-red-500` reads as a pseudo-class), `w-1/2` (`/` needs escaping), `w-[10px]` (`[` starts an attribute selector) or a name starting with a digit.
Fix: Give the element a separate plain class as the event hook and select that: `<button className="save hover:bg-red-500">` with `DOM.click('.save')`. Or use a control. If you do need to match such a class, escape it: `DOM.click('.hover\\:bg-red-500')` in a JavaScript string.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG108

## SYG109

SYG109 (warn): Numeric style value without a unit
Sygnal assigns each key of `style` to `elm.style` as written and does not append `px` (React does; Sygnal deliberately doesn't). For a property that needs a unit, a number is invalid CSS, so `style={{ width: 10 }}` sets nothing, silently. Zero is valid, and so are unitless properties such as `opacity`, `zIndex`, `flexGrow`, `fontWeight`, `lineHeight` and the SVG `strokeWidth` (the list is React's `isUnitlessNumber`, plus the few CSS number properties React's list misses). Custom properties (`--x`) are never reported, and `delayed`, `remove` and `destroy` sub-objects are checked too.
Fix: Write a string with the unit: `style={{ width: '10px' }}` (or `` `${state.w}px` ``). `sygnal-check --fix` rewrites a number literal to `'10px'`, except for time and angle properties such as `transitionDuration` or `rotate`, where the unit is yours to choose.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG109

## SYG110

SYG110 (warn): Intent selector not present in the component view
A class or id selector used in the intent (`DOM.select('.x')`, `DOM.click('.x')`, ...) is never rendered by the component's own view, nor by JSX passed into it as children/slots, so the action never fires. For a control (`DOM.click(Add)`), the view never renders `<Add>`. It is reported as info instead of warn when a dynamic `className`/`id` in the view might produce the name, or when the selector itself is not a static string and could not be checked.
Fix: Fix the selector to match the view, or add the class/id to the element, e.g. `className="x"`; use a string literal (or module-level const) selector so it can be checked. For a control, render it in the view (`<Add>Add</Add>`) or listen to a control the view does render. For a CSS Module class, keep a stable hook class beside it (``className={`save ${s.save}`}``), listen to a control, or select the hashed name (``DOM.click(`.${s.save}`)``).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG110

## SYG111

SYG111 (warn): Controlled input has no input listener
An `<input>`, `<textarea>` or `<select>` has `value` (or a checkbox/radio has `checked`) set, but the component's intent has no input/change/keyup/keydown listener on it or an ancestor. Sygnal writes the bound value back on every render, so any re-render while the user is typing or clicking resets the field; this also applies to literal values such as `value=""` and to `value={null}`/`checked={null}`, which clear or uncheck the field on every render (only an absent prop leaves a field uncontrolled). A key listener that is immediately filtered to one key (e.g. Enter) does not count.
Fix: Update state on input, e.g. `DOM.input('.name').value()` (or `DOM.change(...)` for toggles/selects), or drop the `value`/`checked` prop (not set it to `null`) to leave the field uncontrolled and read it on blur or submit.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG111

## SYG112

SYG112 (error): Reply action has no model entry
A request sent to a driver with reply actions (`makeFetchDriver`, `driverFromAsync`, the socket driver) names its reply actions, as in `{ url, ok: 'LOADED', error: 'FAILED' }`, and the driver delivers the reply to the sending component as that action. When the component's model has no entry with that name, the reply is dropped, usually because of a typo, or because the entry is in another component: a reply goes only to the instance that sent the request (two instances, every Collection item), never to a parent that has an entry of that name. The dev entry checks each request with reply actions as it is sent;
Fix: Use the name of an existing model entry (the message names the closest one), or add the entry: `LOADED: (state, body) => ({ ...state, data: body })`. When an ancestor handles the reply, send the request from the ancestor: the child emits `EVENTS: event('RETRY_TEMPLATES')`, the ancestor selects it in its intent and sends the request from that entry, so the reply comes back to it.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG112

## SYG115

SYG115 (warn): Unknown DOM event shorthand
`DOM.<name>(selector)` is shorthand for `DOM.select(selector).events('<name>')`, and the DOM source accepts any property name, so a made-up name such as `DOM.key('.search')`, `DOM.enter(...)` or `DOM.keyDown(...)` listens for an event the browser never fires: the action silently never happens. The dev entry reports a shorthand call whose name is not a known DOM event, once per component and name. Key names and the enriched-stream helpers (`.key()`, `.value()`, `.checked()`, `.data()`) are not events.
Fix: Use the real event and an enriched-stream helper: `DOM.keydown('.search').key()` (add `.filter(k => k === 'Enter')` for one key), `DOM.input('.name').value()`, `DOM.change('.box').checked()`. For a custom event you dispatch yourself, use the explicit form `DOM.select(sel).events('my-event')`, which is never reported.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG115

## SYG116

SYG116 (error): EVENTS value has no string type
A model sent a value without a string `type` to the `EVENTS` sink, so no `EVENTS.select(type)` can receive it and it is dropped. The usual cause is a function: a model entry that returns `event(...)` (for example `{ EVENTS: () => event('SAVED', data) }`) instead of being `event(...)`, or any other reducer that returns a function. Each emitted value is copied into a new object, so a function arrives on the bus as `{}`. A reducer that returns `undefined` or `null` (see SYG217) causes it too. `sygnal-check` reports a sink entry that is a function returning `event(...)` (or `emit(...)`) from 'sygnal' (ui-sweep R5).
Fix: Make `event()` the sink entry itself: `SAVE: { EVENTS: event('SAVED', (state, data) => payload) }`; return `ABORT` from a reducer to send nothing.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG116

## SYG117

SYG117 (warn): next() names an action with no model entry
`next('X')` in a model handler dispatches `X` to the same component, and only there. When that component has no model entry `X`, nothing happens: no error, no state change. The usual cause is a child calling `next()` for an action its parent handles (a card's `next('ENTER')` when only the page has `ENTER`), which looks like a hang; a typo is the other. The dev entry reports the first `next()` of each name a component sends with no entry, and names the nearest ancestor that has one.
Fix: To reach the parent, send the action up: give the entry a `PARENT` sink (`PARENT: (state) => ({ … })`) and read it in the parent's intent with `ENTER: CHILD.select(Card)`, or emit `EVENTS: event('ENTER', …)` and select it there. For a typo, use the existing entry's name; otherwise add the entry to this component's model.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG117

## SYG118

SYG118 (warn): Host intent replaces a behavior trigger
An intent action named like a behavior action (`'tabs.SELECT'`, `'profile.OPEN'`) replaces the trigger the behavior builds for it; it doesn't add one. When that trigger comes from an option you passed (`tabs({ tab: '.tab' })` makes `tabs.SELECT` from clicks on `.tab`; `dialog({ trigger: '.edit' })` makes `profile.OPEN` from clicks on `.edit`), the elements the option names stop working: tab clicks no longer select, the trigger no longer opens the dialog.
Fix: To add another element, list both in the option (`trigger: '.edit, .avatar'`, `tab: '.tab, .go-billing'`), or give the other element its own action that dispatches the behavior's with `next('profile.OPEN')`, or write the slice in a reducer (`{ ...state, tabs: { ...state.tabs, selected: 'billing' } }`). To replace the trigger on purpose, leave the option out.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG118

## SYG124

SYG124 (error): Component used as a control or selector
A component was passed where `DOM.select()` or a `DOM.<event>()` shorthand expects a control or a CSS selector, as in `DOM.click(TodoItem)`. A component is not an element: it has no single root to listen on, and its elements are isolated from the parent, so there is nothing for the listener to match. Controls look like components in JSX, which makes this an easy mistake.
Fix: Handle the event inside the child and send it up with `PARENT`, then read it in the parent with `CHILD.select(TodoItem)`. Or give the parent a control and render it around the child: `const { Item } = controls({ Item: 'div' })`, `<Item><TodoItem /></Item>`, `DOM.click(Item)`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG124

## SYG125

SYG125 (error): Control given .intent, .model or .initialState
A control from `controls({ ... })` was given `.intent`, `.model` or `.initialState`, as if it were a component. Controls are elements, not components: a control renders its element with a `data-control` marker and nothing else, so it has no intent, model or state, and these statics are never used.
Fix: Put the intent and model on the component that renders the control, and listen to the control there: `App.intent = ({ DOM }) => ({ ADD: DOM.click(Add) })`. For something with its own state and actions, write a component instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG125

## SYG126

SYG126 (info): Control rendered but never listened to
A component renders a control (for example `<Add>`), but its intent never listens to it. A control exists to link an element to an intent, so an unused one is usually a missing intent entry or a leftover from a refactor. A control the model sends element commands to (`ELEMENT: { showModal: HelpDialog }`) counts as used. It is info because a control may also be used only to find the element in tests (`t.query(Draft)`).
Fix: Listen to it in the component's intent (`ADD: DOM.click(Add)`), or render the plain element (`<button>`) if it needs no events.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG126

## SYG127

SYG127 (error): Behavior collision or unresolvable uses entry
A component's `uses` static names behaviors: `TaskList.uses = { pager: pager({ pageSize: 10, next: Newer }) }` runs the behavior on `state.pager`, with its actions named `pager.NEXT`. Three things break that. The host's `initialState` already has the key (`initialState = { pager: ... }`): the behavior's slice replaces it, so the host's value is lost. A `uses` value is not what a `defineBehavior()` factory returns (a plain object, the factory itself without the call, `undefined`): it is skipped, so `state[key]` and its actions never exist.
Fix: Remove the key from the host's `initialState` (set the behavior's values through its options: `pager({ pageSize: 10 })`), or rename the `uses` key. For an unresolvable entry, call the factory: `uses = { pager: pager() }`, with `pager = defineBehavior({ ... })`. For an unknown option, use the name the behavior reads (the message lists them and suggests the closest).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG127

## SYG128

SYG128 (error): Duplicate control key
Two `controls()` calls in one file declare the same key, or one call repeats a key. Every control renders `data-control="<Key>"` and is selected by that key, so two controls with one key match each other's elements: a listener on one also fires for the other.
Fix: Rename one of the keys, or declare both controls in a single `controls({ ... })` call.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG128

## SYG129

SYG129 (warn): CHILD.select() of a component this one doesn't render
An intent reads `CHILD.select(TaskRow)`, but the component's view doesn't render `TaskRow`: a component it renders does (a grandchild, for example a Collection item inside a child). A component's `PARENT` output reaches only the component that renders it, so the action never fires and nothing says why. sygnal-check follows the views it can read and reports the chain (`App > ProjectSection > TaskRow`).
Fix: Relay the value through the component in between: in `ProjectSection.intent` read `RELAY: CHILD.select(TaskRow)`, in `ProjectSection.model` send it on with `RELAY: { PARENT: (state, data) => data }`, and read `CHILD.select(ProjectSection)` in `App`. For a value many components need, broadcast it with `EVENTS` instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG129

## SYG130

SYG130 (error): href() names no route or leaves out a param
`router.href(name, params)` builds a link from the route table passed to `makeRouter({ routes })`. When `name` is not a route (or is the `'*'` not-found route), href() returns the app's root path; when the pattern has a `:param` that `params` leaves out, that segment is empty (`/tasks/`). Either way the link goes somewhere else than intended. The `sygnal/diagnostics` dev entry checks every href() call; production builds don't. A `{ to }` command with the same problem is SYG620.
Fix: Use a route name from the table (the message suggests the closest one) and pass every param the pattern names: `href('task', { id: task.id })`.

## SYG131

SYG131 (warn): Route params the pattern does not use
An href() call or a `{ to, params }` router command passes a param that the route's pattern has no `:name` for. It is ignored, so the value never reaches the URL; usually it was meant for the query string, or the route is the wrong one.
Fix: Pass only the pattern's params, and put other values in the query: `href('tasks', {}, { page: 2 })` or `{ to: 'tasks', query: { page: 2 } }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG131

## SYG132

SYG132 (warn): Declaration static that is never sent
Declaration statics (`route`, `resources`, `connections`, `head`) are computed from the component's state and sent to their driver whenever they change, with or without a model. A root component (the one passed to `run()`) with a model but no `initialState` has no state, so its state stream never emits: the route never arrives, the resources never load, the connections never open, the head never changes. Sub-components share their parent's state, so this only happens at the root.
Fix: Give the root an `initialState`, even an empty object; for the router, seed the route: `App.initialState = { route: router.current() }`. Don't add an `initialState` to a sub-component that shares its parent's state: it would replace that state (SYG405).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG132

## SYG133

SYG133 (warn): SPA router inside a Vike app
`makeRouter()` intercepts link clicks and writes the history itself, and so does Vike's client router. Running the SPA router inside a Vike app makes both handle each click and navigation. In Vike, give the router Vike's `navigate()`: it then leaves links and history to Vike, navigates with `navigate()`, and re-reads the route after each Vike navigation.
Fix: `makeRouter({ routes, navigate })` with `import { navigate } from 'vike/client/router'`, using a route table that mirrors the Vike routes; or read the route from Vike's page context and drop the router.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG133

## SYG140

SYG140 (warn): Widget dispatched an undeclared event
A widget made with `defineWidget()` called `dispatch(name, detail)` (the third parameter of `mount`) with a name that is not in its `events` list. The event is still dispatched (a bubbling `CustomEvent` on the host), but `events` is what the docs, sygnal-check and the other widget diagnostics read: a listener for the declared name never hears this one, which is usually a typo (`dispatch('chnage', d)`) or a declaration that was never added. The dev entry reports it once per widget and name when it is dispatched; sygnal-check reports a literal `dispatch('x')` inside `mount()` (whatever the parameter is called) when `events` is a literal list.
Fix: Add the name to the widget's `events` (`defineWidget({ events: ['pick', 'clear'], ... })`), or dispatch one of the declared names.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG140

## SYG141

SYG141 (warn): Listener for an event the widget does not declare
The intent listens for an event on a widget's host (`DOM.select('.due').events('pikc')`, or a widget control: `DOM.select(Due).events('pikc')`) that the widget doesn't list in its `events`, that no element fires natively, and that is a near-typo of a declared event, so the action most likely never fires. sygnal-check resolves the selector through the static `className` and `id` of the elements the component's own view renders: it reports only when every element with that class or id is a widget host and the widgets' `events` are literal lists.
Fix: Listen for the declared event the name is close to (`DOM.select('.due').events('pick').detail()`), or add the name to the widget's `events` and dispatch it from `mount()`. On a Select or Combobox: `DOM.select('.size').events('value-change').detail()`; on a Menu: `events('select')`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG141

## SYG142

SYG142 (error): Widget command not declared
An element command (`ELEMENT: { open: '.due' }`) reached a widget's host, but the widget declares no command of that name and the host element has no such method, so it can't run (for a non-widget element this is SYG641). The message lists the commands the widget declares. A widget's declared command wins over a native method of the same name (`focus` runs the widget's `focus`; `close` and `togglePopover` too, with the options object). The dev entry reports it when the command reaches the element.
Fix: Send one of the widget's commands, or add the command to its definition: `defineWidget({ commands: { open: (instance, options) => instance.open() } })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG142

## SYG143

SYG143 (warn): Widget tag used as a selector
The tag `defineWidget()` returned was used where a selector is expected: `DOM.select(DatePicker)`, `DOM.click(DatePicker)`, `ELEMENT: { open: DatePicker }` or inside a template string. A widget tag is a JSX tag, not a selector (several hosts of the same widget may render), so it matches nothing and the action never fires. The dev entry reports it once per widget; sygnal-check reports it for intent selectors and element command targets.
Fix: Give the widget a `className` and select that: `<DatePicker className="due" />` with `DOM.select('.due').events('pick')` and `ELEMENT: { open: '.due' }`. Or make it a control (the alternative form): `const { Due } = controls({ Due: DatePicker })`, then `DOM.select(Due)` and `{ open: Due }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG143

## SYG144

SYG144 (info): Widget event the host element also fires natively
A widget declares an event whose name the browser also uses (`'change'`, `'input'`, `'select'`, `'toggle'`...). Native events of that name fire on the host or bubble up from inside it (flatpickr's own input fires `change` as well), so a listener on the host gets both the widget's `CustomEvent` and the native event, and `.detail()` is `undefined` for the native one. Information only: it may be what you want. The dev entry reports it once per widget when a host mounts (names the host element knows as `on<name>`); sygnal-check reports the literal `events` entries it recognises.
Fix: Give the widget's event its own name (`'pick'` for a date picker's selection, `'rate'` for a rating) and emit that, or make the listener handle both (`.filter((e) => e instanceof CustomEvent)`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG144

## SYG145

SYG145 (warn): Sortable item without its id attribute
The `sortable` behavior finds the item a pointer press or a key is on with `event.target.closest(item)` and reads its id from the item element's `attr` attribute (`data-id` by default), then looks that id up in `state[from]` (by `idField`, `id` by default). An item element without the attribute can't be matched to an entry of the list, so the press or key is ignored and the item can't be moved. Usually the item renders its id under another attribute name, or the `item` selector matches an element inside the one that carries the id. Reported once per `item` selector, at the first press or key on such an item.
Fix: Render the id on the item element (`<li className="task" data-id={state.id}>`), point `item` at the element that carries it, or name the attribute: `sortable({ from: 'tasks', item: '.task', attr: 'data-key' })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG145

## SYG146

SYG146 (warn): Sortable item or handle selector matches nothing
At the host's first pointer press or key press, the `sortable` behavior checks its selectors against what the host rendered (its children and Collection items included): `item` is reported when elements carry the id attribute (`attr`) but none matches `item`, and `handle` when items exist but none contains an element matching `handle`. Either way no item can be picked up, by pointer or keyboard. An empty list can't tell a typo from no items, so the check waits for a later interaction. Reported once per selector.
Fix: Use the selector of the elements the items render: `item: '.task'` for `<li className="task" data-id={id}>`, `handle: '.grip'` for the drag handle inside it, or leave `handle` out to drag the whole item.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG146

## SYG147

SYG147 (warn): Sortable list key is not an array in the host state
`sortable({ from })` reorders `state[from]` (each key of an array `from` for moves between lists). When the host starts, a `from` key whose value is missing or not an array is reported: nothing in it can be found, so no item can be moved. The message suggests a close array key of the state when there is one. Reported once per key; a list that arrives later should start as an empty array.
Fix: Name the array in the host's state (`from: 'tasks'` for `initialState: { tasks: [...] }`), and start a list that is loaded later as `[]`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG147

## SYG148

SYG148 (warn): Collection viewTransitionName is not a CSS identifier
A `<Collection>` or `<VirtualCollection>` has a `viewTransitionName` that is not a string starting a CSS identifier (a letter, `_`, `-` followed by a letter or `_`, or `--`; then letters, digits, `-` and `_`). Each item's name is `<prefix>-<id>`, so with a prefix such as `'1card'`, `'my card'` or `'card.x'` every name is invalid CSS: the browser ignores the `view-transition-name` and nothing animates, with no error. The dev entry reports it once per component and prefix when the Collection renders. An empty string, `0` or `false` names no item and is not reported.
Fix: Use a CSS identifier as the prefix: `viewTransitionName="card"` (letters, digits, `-` and `_`, not starting with a digit). The ids are escaped for you.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG148

## SYG149

SYG149 (warn): Two items with the same view-transition name
After a render, two rendered elements on the page (not in a `display: none` subtree, such as a hidden tab panel: the browser doesn't capture those) have the same `view-transition-name` from Collections with the same `viewTransitionName` prefix: the same item `id` is in two of them at once (an 'All' list and a 'Favorites' list both named `card`). A name must be unique when a View Transition starts, so the browser skips the whole transition (Chromium logs `Unexpected duplicate view-transition-name`). The same prefix on several Collections is meant for one item moving between them, never shown in two at once.
Fix: Give Collections that can show the same item at the same time different prefixes (`viewTransitionName="all"` and `viewTransitionName="fav"`), or set the item's own `style={{ viewTransitionName }}` where it needs one.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG149

## SYG150

SYG150 (warn): Agent action has no model entry
A component's `agent` declaration (sygnal/ai) lists an action under `actions` that the component's `model` has no entry for (and no behavior of its `uses` owns). The agent layer offers it as a tool, and every call dispatches an action nothing handles, so the call fails with "changed nothing" and the model retries or gives up. Usually a typo, or an entry renamed on one side only. sygnal-check reports it when the declaration and the model are object literals it can read (no spreads), and suggests the closest model entry. TypeScript catches it only when every key is wrong.
Fix: Rename the key to the model entry it means (`actions: { ADD: { description: 'Add a todo', input } }` for `model.ADD`), or add the model entry: `TodoApp.model = { ..., ADD: (state, text) => ({ ...state, todos: [...state.todos, { id: state.nextId, text }] }) }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG150

## SYG151

SYG151 (warn): Misspelled agent static
A component has a static named like the agent declaration but spelled differently: `agents`, `tools`, `Agent`, `tool`. The agent layer (the chat behavior, WebMCP, the command bar, `t.tools()`) reads only `Component.agent`, so the component offers no tools and its `read` projection never reaches the model, without any error. Reported on a component (a function with other Sygnal statics) or on an object with `actions` or `read`.
Fix: Rename the static: `TodoApp.agent = { name: 'todos', description: 'The todo list', read: (state) => ({ todos: state.todos }), actions: { ADD: { description: 'Add a todo', input: z.string() } } }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG151

## SYG152

SYG152 (warn): LLM request without an ok action
A model sends an LLM request (an object with `messages`, sent to the chat driver of sygnal/ai) that names no `ok` reply action. The driver delivers the finished reply (the assistant `message`, its `text`, `toolCalls`, `finishReason` and `usage`) only as the `ok` action, so the reply is lost: a `delta` action shows the text while it streams, but the final message never reaches the state and the status never leaves streaming. sygnal-check follows requests that local helpers build; a request with a spread (`{ ...base, messages }`) is not reported, since the spread may name `ok`.
Fix: Name the actions the reply arrives as, and handle them: `LLM: (state) => ({ messages: state.messages, delta: 'DELTA', ok: 'DONE', error: 'FAILED' })` with `DONE: (state, { message }) => ({ ...state, messages: [...state.messages, message], draft: '' })`. For a whole conversation with tools, the `chat` behavior does this for you.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG152

## SYG153

SYG153 (warn): WebMCP form attribute set as a DOM property
A `<form>` has `toolname`, `tooldescription` or `toolautosubmit` (or a field has `toolparamdescription`) written as a plain JSX attribute. WebMCP's declarative API reads these as HTML attributes, but Sygnal's JSX pragma turns an attribute it doesn't know into a DOM property (`form.toolname = ...`), which the browser ignores: the form is never offered to the browser's agent, and nothing reports it at run time.
Fix: For a form with the `form` behavior, give it a tool and let it write every attribute: `form(schema, { values, submit: 'SIGN_UP', tool: formTool({ name: 'sign_up', description: 'Create an account' }) })` with `formTool` from `sygnal/ai` (experimental; each field's `<label>`, then its `aria-label`, becomes its `toolparamdescription`). Otherwise write them as attributes: `<form attrs-toolname="sign_up" attrs-tooldescription="Create an account">` and `<input name="email" attrs-toolparamdescription="The email to sign up with" />` (or `attrs={{ toolname: 'sign_up' }}`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG153

## SYG160

SYG160 (warn): Result part rendered outside a card
A part declared with `result: true` in `defineCatalog({ parts })` (sygnal/ai) answers a card: the `chat` behavior's `ask_user` tool shows a card built from the catalog, and the result part sends `compose.answer(props, value)` to PARENT, which the chat hears with `CHILD.select` and turns into the tool call's output. The answer names the card by `props.scope`, the tool call id that `askCard(catalog, state, part)` passes to `catalog.render`. Here a result part was rendered with no scope (by a `compose` page, or by `catalog.render` called without `scope`), so its answer has nowhere to go: no tool call waits for it.
Fix: Render cards with `askCard(catalog, state, part)` for each `tool-ask_user` part of the chat's messages. On a composed page, use a part without `result: true`, or a separate catalog for the page and for the cards.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG160

## SYG161

SYG161 (error): Catalog container render is a component with a model
A container in `defineCatalog({ containers })` (sygnal/ai) is a view function: `catalog.render()` calls its `render` inline with `{ key, node, slots, children, ui, control }`, so the composed parts stay children of the component that renders the composition. Its `render` here is a component (it has a `model`, `intent`, `initialState` or `uses`). A component would own the parts placed in its slots: the host's `CHILD.select(Part)` would stop hearing them, their lenses would start from the container's state, and a part moved out of it would be re-created. The function is still called as a view, so its model, intent and state never run.
Fix: Make `render` a plain function of its argument (`render: ({ children, ui, control }) => <Tabs ...>`), and keep container state in `ui` with `control(name, value)` (a click on the element sets `ui[key][name]`). Put stateful UI inside a part instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG161

## SYG162

SYG162 (error): Catalog part with neither component nor render
Every part in `defineCatalog({ parts })` (sygnal/ai) needs something to render: a `component` (a Sygnal component, rendered as a child of the host with its lens, params and props) or a `render` view function (called inline with the same props). This part has neither, usually a misspelled key or an import that resolved to undefined. It stays in the catalog, so layouts that name it are valid, but it renders nothing. Reported in development, when the catalog is defined; `sygnal-check` reports a literal part declaration (without a spread) that has neither key.
Fix: Add `component: MyPart` (check the import) or `render: (props) => <div>…</div>`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG162

## SYG170

SYG170 (warn): Context field read with no provider
A component reads `context.theme` (in its view, or in a reducer through `props.context`), but neither it nor any component above it has `theme` in its `.context`, so the value is `undefined`. Context flows down the render tree: a component sees what it and its ancestors declare. sygnal-check follows every way up from the reader and reports only when each ends at a component that `run()` or `defineElement()` starts, so it knows the whole chain.
Fix: Add the field to the `.context` of the reader or a component above it: `App.context = { theme: (state) => state.theme }`. If the name is misspelled (the message suggests the closest one on the chain), fix the read.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG170

## SYG171

SYG171 (warn): PARENT sink no parent reads
A component's model sends to `PARENT`, but none of the components that render it reads `CHILD.select(It)` in its intent. A `PARENT` value reaches only the component that renders it, through `CHILD.select`, so here every value goes nowhere and the click does nothing. sygnal-check reports it when the parents render it by tag, as a Collection item or as a Switchable target, no scanned intent selects it (a select in the wrong component is SYG129), and it can read every parent's intent: one with `uses` (a behavior may read `CHILD`), a sources rest pattern, `CHILD` passed to a helper, or a `CHILD.select()` it can't resolve keeps it silent.
Fix: Read it in the parent's intent and handle it in the model: `App.intent = ({ CHILD }) => ({ PICK: CHILD.select(Badge) })` with `App.model = { PICK: (state, data) => ... }`. If nothing needs the value, remove the `PARENT` sink; for components further apart, use `EVENTS`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG171

## SYG201

SYG201 (warn): STATE reducer dropped keys from the previous state
A STATE reducer returned a plain object that is missing keys present (and not `undefined`) in the previous state, which usually means a missing `...state` spread. Those keys are silently lost from state. Calculated fields, `INITIALIZE` and internal `__*` actions are excluded; reported once per component and action.
Fix: Spread the previous state: `(state, data) => ({ ...state, field: data })`. If removing the keys is intended, ignore the warning.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG201

## SYG202

SYG202 (warn): STATE reducer returned undefined
A STATE reducer returned `undefined`, typically from a block-bodied arrow function without `return`. In a root component this wipes the state (a warning). Returning `undefined` from a Collection item's reducer is the documented way to remove the item, so it is not reported there; in another sub-component (a child rendered by tag) it is reported as info. `INITIALIZE` and internal `__*` actions are excluded.
Fix: Return the new state, e.g. `(state, data) => ({ ...state, ... })`, or return `ABORT` to leave the state unchanged.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG202

## SYG204

SYG204 (warn): Root component has no state, so its view never renders
The core calls a component's view only while its state is defined. A root component gets its first state from `initialState`, from an `INITIALIZE` reducer, or, with no model at all, renders without one. A root that has a model but no `initialState` starts with `undefined` state, so nothing is rendered: no error, an empty page, and a `DOM.click()` intent that can never fire because its element never appears. Generated code that has no data of its own often looks like this.
Fix: Give the root an `initialState`, `App.initialState = {}` when it has no data of its own, or return the first state from an `INITIALIZE` reducer. To show a loading state before data arrives, start from one (`{ loading: true }`) rather than from no state.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG204

## SYG206

SYG206 (error): Invalid calculated field definition
An entry in `calculated` is neither a function nor a two-element `[deps, fn]` array where `deps` is an array and `fn` is a function. The component constructor throws, so the component is never created.
Fix: Define each field as `state => value` or `[['a', 'b'], state => value]`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG206

## SYG207

SYG207 (warn): Calculated field shadows an initialState key
A key in `calculated` also exists in `initialState`. The calculated value overwrites the stored value of the same name, so the `initialState` value is never visible. Checked once when the component is constructed.
Fix: Rename either the calculated field or the `initialState` key.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG207

## SYG208

SYG208 (warn): Calculated field depends on an unknown key
A calculated field declared as `[deps, fn]` lists a dependency that is neither another calculated field nor a key of `initialState`. The dependency is likely misspelled, so memoization compares an always-`undefined` value. Only checked when the component has an `initialState`.
Fix: Fix the dependency name, or add the key to `initialState`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG208

## SYG209

SYG209 (error): Circular calculated field dependency
Calculated fields declared with `[deps, fn]` depend on each other in a cycle (the message shows the path, e.g. `a -> b -> a`), so no evaluation order exists. The component constructor throws.
Fix: Break the cycle so that each calculated field depends only on state keys or on fields that do not depend back on it.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG209

## SYG210

SYG210 (warn): INITIALIZE used with a sink other than STATE
The model defines `INITIALIZE` as an object with sinks other than the state sink (e.g. `EVENTS` or `EFFECT`). `INITIALIZE` only supports the state sink, so those other sink entries are deleted and never run.
Fix: Keep only `STATE` under `INITIALIZE` and move the other sinks to a different action (for example one triggered by `BOOTSTRAP` or via `next()`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG210

## SYG211

SYG211 (error): Retired in 6.0: Invalid model shorthand entry
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. Before 6.0 it was thrown for a malformed `'ACTION | SINK'` model key (one that did not split into an action and a sink). Sygnal 6.0 removed those keys (the object form is the only form), so there is nothing to split; a removed key is reported as SYG612 (dev) and SYG504 (`sygnal-check --strict`).
Fix: Use the object form: `SAVE: { EFFECT: (state, data, next) => … }`. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#pipe-keys.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG211

## SYG212

SYG212 (error): Model entry is not a function or an object of sinks
A model entry's value is neither a function (a STATE reducer) nor a plain object mapping sink names to reducers; for example a string, number, array or `null`. Model setup throws when the component is initialized.
Fix: Use a reducer function or a sink map, e.g. `{ STATE: (state) => ..., EVENTS: ... }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG212

## SYG213

SYG213 (warn): Retired in 6.0: Duplicate model entry for the same action and sink
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. Before 6.0 it warned when an `'ACTION | SINK'` key and an object-form entry defined the same action and sink. With the shorthand keys removed in 6.0, an action/sink pair can be defined only once.
Fix: Nothing to change. Use one object-form entry per action: `SAVE: { STATE: …, EFFECT: … }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG213

## SYG214

SYG214 (error): EFFECT handler threw
A model entry on the `EFFECT` sink threw an exception. The error is caught and logged with `console.error` (with the original error attached) rather than thrown, so the app keeps running but the effect did not complete. In diagnostics `error` mode the diagnostic is rethrown asynchronously. If the exception is itself a coded Sygnal error (for example SYG215 from `next()`), it is reported under that code instead.
Fix: Fix the exception shown in the attached error, or guard the handler against missing state or data.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG214

## SYG215

SYG215 (error): next() delay is not a number
The third argument of `next(type, data, delay)` was given and is not a number. `next()` throws and the follow-up action is not dispatched. When it is called inside a reducer or EFFECT handler, the handler catches the throw and reports it under this code (not SYG216 or SYG214), so a STATE reducer leaves the state unchanged and a driver-sink reducer sends nothing.
Fix: Pass a number of milliseconds, or omit it for the default 10 ms: `next('ACTION', data, 100)`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG215

## SYG216

SYG216 (error): Reducer threw
A model reducer threw an exception. For a STATE reducer the error is logged and the state is left unchanged; for a driver sink (e.g. `EVENTS`, `PARENT`, custom drivers) it is logged and nothing is sent. The error is logged with `console.error` rather than thrown (rethrown asynchronously in diagnostics `error` mode). A coded Sygnal error thrown inside the reducer (for example SYG215 from `next()`) is reported under its own code instead.
Fix: Fix the exception shown in the attached error, or guard the reducer against missing state or data.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG216

## SYG217

SYG217 (warn): Driver-sink reducer returned undefined
A reducer for a non-STATE sink (e.g. `EVENTS`, `PARENT` or a custom driver) returned `undefined`, often from a missing `return`. The `undefined` value is still sent to the driver.
Fix: Return the value the driver expects, or return `ABORT` to send nothing.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG217

## SYG218

SYG218 (error): Reducer returned an unsupported type
A reducer for a non-STATE sink (e.g. `EVENTS`, `PARENT` or a custom driver) returned a symbol other than `ABORT`. Any other value, including `null`, arrays and bigints, is sent to the driver as-is, like a constant sink value. It is logged with `console.error` (not thrown) and nothing is sent.
Fix: Return the value the driver expects, or return `ABORT` to send nothing.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG218

## SYG219

SYG219 (warn): EFFECT handler returned a value
An `EFFECT` handler returned something other than `undefined`. EFFECT entries run only for side effects, so the return value is ignored; this usually means the logic was meant for a STATE or driver sink. Returning `ABORT` from an EFFECT also triggers it.
Fix: Do not return a value from EFFECT handlers; move value-producing logic to a `STATE` or driver sink entry.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG219

## SYG220

SYG220 (warn): Calculated field threw
A calculated field function threw while computing derived state, for example by reading a property of missing data. The error is caught and the field is skipped for that update, so it is not recomputed from the new state.
Fix: Guard the calculation against missing data, e.g. `state => state.user?.name ?? ''`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG220

## SYG221

SYG221 (error): set() called with a string
`set()` takes an object to merge (`set({ open: true })`) or a function that returns one (`set((state, data) => ({ ... }))`). Called with a field name, `set('city')` spreads the string into the state, adding the keys `'0'`, `'1'`, ... one per character, and the field itself never changes. The dev entry recognises those keys after the reducer runs and reports the field name; TypeScript also rejects a string argument.
Fix: To store the action data in a field, pass a function: `set((state, city) => ({ city }))`. For a fixed value pass an object: `set({ city: 'Paris' })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG221

## SYG222

SYG222 (warn): STATE reducer returned the same object after it was mutated in place
A STATE reducer changed the state object it received (`state.count++`, `state.done = true`, `delete state.x`) and returned that same object. Since 6.0 a reducer that returns the object it got means "no change" (the same as `ABORT`), so the change is ignored: no state is emitted and nothing re-renders. The dev entry takes a shallow snapshot of the state (its keys and top-level values) before each STATE reducer runs and compares it when the reducer returns the same object; the report names the changed keys. Mutations below the top level (`state.items.push(x)`) are not seen. In production the mutation is silently ignored.
Fix: Return a new object: `INC: (state) => ({ ...state, count: state.count + 1 })`. To write updates as mutations, wrap the reducer in immer's `produce()`: `INC: produce((draft) => { draft.count++ })`, which returns a new object when something changed and the same object when nothing did.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG222

## SYG223

SYG223 (warn): persist pick or omit names a key that is not in initialState
`App.persist = persist({ key, pick, omit })` saves the top-level state keys listed in `pick` (or every key except those in `omit`). A name in either list that is not a key of the component's `initialState` (or of its `uses`: a behavior's slice, such as `chat`, is a state key too) is usually a typo or a renamed key: with `pick` that key is never saved (and never restored), with `omit` the key you meant to leave out is saved after all. The dev entry reports it when the root component is created; sygnal-check reports it statically when the options and `initialState` are literals, with the closest key as a suggestion.
Fix: Use top-level keys of `initialState` or `uses`: `persist({ key: 'todo-app', pick: ['todos', 'filter'] })`, or add the key to `initialState`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG223

## SYG224

SYG224 (error): persist on a component that is not the root
`persist({ ... })` is set up by the root component only (the one passed to `run()` or `renderComponent()`): it saves and restores the app's whole state tree, and a sub-component's state is a slice of it. On any other component the `persist` static is ignored, so nothing is saved or restored. In Vike, a Page, Layout or Wrapper rendered in the Layout/Wrapper shell is a sub-component (the shell is the app's root), so `persist` isn't supported there yet, and the message says so; a Vike page with no Layout or Wrapper is its own root, where `persist` works. The dev entry reports it when the component is created;
Fix: Move `persist` to the root component and `pick` the key that holds the sub-component's state: `App.persist = persist({ key: 'app', pick: ['todos'] })` for a child rendered with `state="todos"`. In a Vike Layout/Wrapper shell, remove it and save the state yourself (`STATE.watch` writing to `localStorage`, read back in `BOOTSTRAP`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG224

## SYG226

SYG226 (warn): Undo track, resetOn or coalesce names an unknown action
`undoable(model, { key, track, resetOn, coalesce })` (and the `undo({ ... })` behavior) records changes to `state[key]` made by the actions in `track`, clears the history on the actions in `resetOn`, and groups quick repeats of the actions in `coalesce` into one step. A name in any of these lists that has no model entry never runs, so with `track` its changes are never recorded (undo skips them), with `resetOn` the history is never cleared (after a load, undo would bring back the old document), and with `coalesce` the action meant to be grouped (typing) is recorded one step per change. It is usually a typo or a renamed action.
Fix: Use the name of a model entry (`track: ['TYPE']`, `resetOn: ['LOADED']`, `coalesce: ['TYPE']`), or add the entry to the model. Leave `track` out to record every action that changes `state[key]`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG226

## SYG230

SYG230 (warn): Form field name not in values
The `form` behavior hears `input` and `focusout` on its form element and reads the event target's `name` as a path in `values` (`email`, `addresses.7.city` for the row with id 7). A named field inside the form whose name is not a field of `values` is ignored: its value never reaches `state.form` and it is never validated. It is usually a typo, a renamed field, a row name built with the index instead of the row's `id`, or an input that belongs to something else (a search box) placed inside the form element. Reported once per name, on `input`;
Fix: Name the input after a path in `values` (`name="email"`, or `name={f.email.name}` from `state.form.fields`), add the field to `values`, or move the unrelated input out of the form element. For a field that appears at run time, name it in the `dynamic` option with its start value: `dynamic: (state) => Object.fromEntries(state.lines.map((key) => [key, { amount: '', currency: 'USD' }]))` makes `${key}.amount` a field while the line is there.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG230

## SYG231

SYG231 (error): form() schema is not a Standard Schema
`form(schema, options)` validates with any Standard Schema (https://standardschema.dev): an object with `~standard.validate`, which zod (3.24+), valibot (1.0+), arktype and others provide. Anything else (a plain object of rules, a validator function, an older library's schema with only `parse`) can't validate, so `form()` throws when it is called, with this code in dev; in production the first validation throws a plain TypeError.
Fix: Pass a Standard Schema object: `form(z.object({ email: z.string().email() }), { ... })`, `form(v.object({ ... }), { ... })`, or a hand-written `{ '~standard': { version: 1, vendor: 'app', validate: (values) => ({ value }) | ({ issues: [{ message, path }] }) } }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG231

## SYG232

SYG232 (info): Form submit dropped while one is in progress
A `form.SUBMIT` (the form element's submit, or `simulateAction('form.SUBMIT')`) arrived while `state.form.submitting` was true (a valid submit sent its request and neither `form.DONE` nor `form.ERRORS` has answered it), or while a submit was queued waiting for an async `check` or an async schema. The form drops it, so a double click never sends twice. Only a submit whose model entry sends on the HTTP sink (the `http` option) stays `submitting`; any other submit is done at once.
Fix: Disable the submit button while `state.form.submitting` is true, and answer the submit action with reply actions: `SIGN_UP: { HTTP: (state, values) => ({ url, json: values, ok: 'form.DONE', error: 'form.ERRORS' }) }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG232

## SYG233

SYG233 (warn): Form value missing from the schema output
On a valid submit the form dispatches the `submit` action with the schema's output (trimmed, transformed values), not with `state.form.values`. A top-level key of `values` that the output doesn't have was stripped (or renamed) by the schema, usually because the schema doesn't declare it (`z.object()` and `v.object()` drop unknown keys), so the submit action never gets that field. Reported once per key, and only when every key of the output is a key of `values`: an output with keys of its own comes from a schema that reshapes the values (a `transform` that renames), which is left alone.
Fix: Declare the field in the schema, make the schema keep unknown keys (`z.looseObject`, `v.looseObject`), or remove the field from `values` if it isn't part of the form.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG233

## SYG234

SYG234 (warn): Form submit action has no model entry
`form(schema, { submit: 'SIGN_UP' })` dispatches the host action named by `submit` with the schema's output when a submit is valid. (With `request: { url }` the form sends the valid submit itself and `submit` is optional.) When neither option is given, or the host component has no model entry named by `submit`, a valid submit does nothing visible (the form marks it done, `submitted: true`, and nothing else happens).
Fix: To save to a URL, give the form a request: `form(schema, { values, request: { url: '/api/signup' } })`. Otherwise name a host action the form doesn't define and add it to the model: `submit: 'SIGN_UP'` with `SIGN_UP: { HTTP: (state, values) => ({ url: '/api/signup', method: 'POST', json: values, ok: 'form.DONE', error: 'form.ERRORS' }) }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG234

## SYG235

SYG235 (warn): Form check names an unknown field or sets reply fields
`check: { email: { request, error } }` runs an async check for a field through a driver: the form sends `request(value)` with its own reply action (`ok`/`error` set to `'form.CHECKED_email'`) and `latest: true`, so a newer value's check replaces an older one. A `check` key that isn't a field of `values` never runs (reported when the component is created; not with the `dynamic` option, whose fields may include it), and a request that sets `ok`, `error` or `latest` has them replaced by the form's (reported when the check runs).
Fix: Use a field name from `values` as the key, and return only the request from `request`: `check: { email: { request: (email) => ({ url: '/api/email-free', query: { email } }), error: (body) => !body.free && 'Taken' } }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG235

## SYG236

SYG236 (warn): Form array rows without an id
Field arrays name their fields by row id (`addresses.7.city`), so errors, touched state, server errors and focus stay with a row when another row is removed. An array of objects in `values` whose rows have no `id` falls back to the index, and after a removal the next row inherits the removed row's errors and touched state. `form.ADD` gives new rows the next id itself; the start values need ids too. Reported when the component is created.
Fix: Give each row a unique `id` in `values`: `addresses: [{ id: 1, street: '', city: '' }]`, render rows with a Collection, and name their inputs `addresses.${state.id}.city`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG236

## SYG237
