SYG237 (warn): Two forms in one component listen on the same form selector
Each `form` behavior hears `input`, `focusout` and `submit` on its form element, found by the `form` option inside the host component (default `'form'`). Two `form` uses in one component with the same selector (both left at the default, usually) both match every form element of the view, so typing in one form changes the other's values too (when the names overlap) and each submit is handled by both. Reported when the component is created.
Fix: Give each form element its own class and pass it as the `form` option: `uses = { login: form(loginSchema, { ..., form: '.login' }), news: form(newsSchema, { ..., form: '.news' }) }` with `<form className="login">` and `<form className="news">`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG237

## SYG238

SYG238 (warn): Root component with a model but no initial state
A root component (the one passed to `run()` or `renderComponent()`) has a `model` but no `initialState`, so its state is `undefined` and its view doesn't run: the page (or the test's `t.html()`) stays empty until an action sets the whole state. A root without a model renders anyway (from `initialState`, or with no state), and a child gets its state from its parent, so neither is reported. The state may also come from `renderComponent(C, { initialState })` or an HMR swap; then nothing is reported either. Reported once per component.
Fix: Give the root its start state: `App.initialState = { count: 0 }`. If the state really arrives later (from a request), start from a placeholder such as `{ status: 'loading' }` and render that.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG238

## SYG239

SYG239 (warn): Form schema function returns a new schema for the same state
`form((state) => schema, options)` validates with a schema that depends on the host's state (which fields are required depends on what is on the form). The form calls the function whenever it validates and caches each result per schema object, and it re-validates whenever the function returns another schema.
Fix: Return the same schema object while the rules don't change: memoize it on the part of the state it reads, not on the whole state. For a schema built from a list or a layout in state, cache it per that object: `const schemas = new WeakMap(); const schemaOf = (state) => { if (!schemas.has(state.lines)) schemas.set(state.lines, build(state.lines)); return schemas.get(state.lines) }`, then `form(schemaOf, { ... })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG239

## SYG240

SYG240 (error): Agent action or query input has no JSON Schema form
An `agent.actions` or `agent.queries` entry's `input` must be a Standard Schema that also implements Standard JSON Schema (Zod 4.2+, ArkType 2.1.28+, Valibot wrapped with `toStandardJsonSchema()` from `@valibot/to-json-schema`), or a plain JSON Schema wrapped with `jsonSchema()` from `sygnal/ai`. The agent layer sends the model the input-side JSON Schema and validates every call with the schema before the action or query runs.
Fix: Use a supported schema: `input: z.string().min(1)`, `input: toStandardJsonSchema(v.picklist(['all', 'done']))`, or `input: jsonSchema({ type: 'integer' })`. For Zod Mini keep its validation with `jsonSchema(z.toJSONSchema(s), { validate: s })`. A `Date` can't come from JSON, and Zod's JSON Schema conversion throws for `z.date()` and `z.coerce.date()` alike (the field reaches the model with no schema, SYG243): take an ISO string, `z.iso.datetime()` (convert it in the reducer) or `z.iso.datetime().transform((s) => new Date(s))` (the model sees the string, the action gets a `Date`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG240

## SYG241

SYG241 (error): Agent read, query, when, until or label threw
The agent layer calls a component's `agent.read(state)` (the projection an agent sees), each action's and query's `when(state)` (whether the tool is offered) and `agent.label(state)` (a Collection item's label) with the instance's current state, once per state change, a query's `run(state, input)` when an agent calls it, and an action's `until(state)` while its call waits. One of them threw.
Fix: Make the function total over every state the component can have: guard optional fields (`state.todos?.length ?? 0`), and keep it a pure function of the state it gets.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG241

## SYG242

SYG242 (warn): WebMCP tool over a size budget
`experimentalExposeWebMcp()` keeps every tool inside Chrome's WebMCP budgets, which neither Chrome 153 nor the polyfill enforce: a tool name of at most 30 characters, a description of at most 500, a parameter description of at most 150, and a result of at most 1,500 characters of JSON. Something went over, and it was cut so the agent still gets a usable tool: a long name keeps its first 25 characters plus `_` and a 4-character hash of the whole (so names stay unique), a description or parameter description ends in `…`, and a long result keeps `ok` and `error`, gets `truncated: true`, and carries its `state` as a cut JSON string.
Fix: Shorten the `agent` declaration's `name`, the action names or the `description` texts, or make `read` return a smaller projection (counts and the fields an agent needs, not the whole state). A Collection item tool's key description lists every item's label: a shorter `label` keeps more of them.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG242

## SYG243

SYG243 (warn): Agent action or query input schema converted with losses
Part of an `agent.actions` or `agent.queries` entry's `input` has no JSON Schema form, for example a refinement (Valibot `check`, ArkType `narrow`) or a `Date`, so the library's lossy conversion left it out of the schema the model gets. The model doesn't see that rule, so it may send values that break it; the layer still validates every call with the full schema and returns the issues to the model. Zod drops refinements without saying so, so no warning is possible there. Reported once per action or query.
Fix: Put the rule in the description the model reads (`.describe('at least 2 characters, must contain @')`), or express it with a JSON Schema keyword (`minLength`, `pattern`, `enum`) instead of a refinement. For a date, take an ISO string and convert it in the reducer: `z.iso.datetime()` (Zod), `v.pipe(v.string(), v.isoDateTime())` (Valibot), `'string.date.iso'` (ArkType).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG243

## SYG244

SYG244 (warn): Agent read returns strings, untrusted not declared
WebMCP marks a tool whose results may carry text from users (or other untrusted sources) with `untrustedContentHint`, so the agent treats that text as data, not instructions. `experimentalExposeWebMcp()` takes the hint from the declaration's `untrusted` field.
Fix: Declare it: `untrusted: true` when `read` returns user-entered text (todo texts, names, messages), `untrusted: false` when its strings are only the app's own (enum values, labels the app wrote).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG244

## SYG245

SYG245 (error): form tool option is not made by formTool()
`form(schema, { tool })` (experimental, ) offers the form to the browser's agent as a declarative WebMCP tool, but only when `tool` is made by `formTool({ name, description, autosubmit })` from `sygnal/ai`. The tool code lives in `formTool` so that apps using `form` without a tool don't carry it; the form behavior only calls the hook on the object it is given. A plain `{ name, description }` object has no such hook: the form works as before but writes no `toolname` attributes and answers no agent. Reported once, in development.
Fix: Wrap the object: `import { formTool } from 'sygnal/ai'`, then `form(schema, { values, submit: 'SIGN_UP', tool: formTool({ name: 'sign_up', description: 'Create an account' }) })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG245

## SYG246

SYG246 (error): Agent query is not a synchronous function
An `agent.queries` entry is a read-only tool: its `run(state, input)` gets the component's current state and the validated input and returns the result the model sees, as `{ ok: true, result }`. It runs outside the action queue, so it must be a pure, synchronous function of what it gets: it can't wait for a request, and nothing it does reaches the app's state. This one is not: `run` is missing or not a function (the query is not offered), or it returned a promise (an `async` function, or one that calls `fetch`), so the call fails with `{ ok: false, error }`. Reported once per query while an agent layer runs.
Fix: Compute the result from `state` and `input` and return it: `run: (state, { customer }) => state.invoices.filter((i) => i.customer === customer)`. For data that has to be fetched, use an action instead: its model entry sets what to load (a `resources` entry or a driver request), and `until: 'resourceName'` on the action makes the call answer with the component's `read` once the data has arrived.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG246

## SYG247

SYG247 (warn): Agent query has the tool name of an action
Actions and queries of one `agent` declaration share its tool-name space: each becomes the tool `<name>_<key>`, with the key in snake case (`FIND` and `find` both give `orders_find`). This query's tool name is already taken by one of the declaration's actions, so the action keeps it and the query is not offered. Reported once per query while an agent layer runs; sygnal-check reports it before the app runs.
Fix: Rename the query so its key names what it returns (`queries: { search: … }` next to an action `FIND`), or remove the duplicate.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG247

## SYG248

SYG248 (warn): Agent action until names no resource
An `agent.actions` entry's `until` makes the call wait for the action's result: a string names one of the component's `resources`, and the call answers once that resource is neither loading nor refreshing. This string names no resource of the component (a typo, a resource declared on another component, or a component with no `resources`), so there is nothing to wait for: the call answers at once, with the state right after the action, as without `until`. Reported once per action while an agent layer runs; sygnal-check reports it before the app runs when the component's `resources` is an object literal.
Fix: Name a key of the component's own `resources` (`until: 'search'` for `resources = { search: (state) => … }`), or pass a function for a result that arrives through a reply action: `until: (state) => state.status !== 'loading'`, with the action's own reducer setting `status: 'loading'`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG248

## SYG250

SYG250 (warn): Layout names an unknown part or slot
A composition's layout (sygnal/ai `compose`, `catalog.finish()`, `catalog.render()`) names a part or container the catalog doesn't have, a slot its container doesn't declare, or a node key that isn't one of its nodes. It usually comes from `SET_LAYOUT` with a hand-made layout, a layout restored by `persist` after the catalog changed, or a model's typo. The node is dropped (the children of an unknown container or slot take its place, so the parts it held survive) and the rest of the layout is used. The same code reports a part's `companions` entry that names no part (ignored). Reported in development;
Fix: Use the catalog's part and container ids and the slot names the container declares. For a persisted layout, bump the `persist` version (or `migrate` the old layout) when you rename or remove parts.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG250

## SYG251

SYG251 (warn): Invalid param value in a layout
A node's `params` don't fit the part's declaration: a value that isn't one of the param's `options`, a number that isn't a number (or is outside `min` … `max`: clamped), text or a list of the wrong type, a list shorter than its `min`, or a param the part doesn't declare. The default is used instead. A node whose record param names no current record (`from(state)` doesn't list it), or whose required `type: 'text'` / `'list'` param (with no default) is missing, can't be shown and is dropped. Over-long text and list items are cut to `maxLength` silently. Reported in development, by the finishing step (`SET_LAYOUT`, `REMOVE`, and both backends).
Fix: Send values the declaration allows (`params: { range: 'quarter' }` for `options: { week, month, quarter }`), and record ids `from(state)` returns. When records can disappear, expect their nodes to go.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG251

## SYG252

SYG252 (warn): Record param from() does not return an array of { value }
A record param (`params: { id: { from: (state) => records } }`) turns app state into one option per record: a decision backend offers each record as a choice, an LLM backend lists them as an enum, and the record's `value` becomes the node key (`project:7`). `from` must return an array of `{ value, name?, aliases?, description? }` with a string or number `value`. It returned something else (or threw), so the part has no records (entries without a valid `value` are skipped). Reported in development, once per part and catalog.
Fix: Return `state.projects.map((p) => ({ value: p.id, name: p.name, description: `${p.name}: ${p.status}` }))`, and guard against missing state (`(state.projects || []).map(…)`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG252

## SYG253

SYG253 (warn): Misspelled catalog declaration key
A key of a `defineCatalog({...})` declaration (sygnal/ai), of a part, a container or a param is one letter or a swap away from a key `defineCatalog` reads (`descrption`, `compnent`, `deafult`, `maxuses`). `defineCatalog` ignores keys it doesn't know, so the setting has no effect: a misspelled `description` leaves the model with only the part's id, a misspelled `default` makes the first option the default, a misspelled `component` renders nothing (SYG162). Other unknown keys are not reported: an app may keep its own data on a declaration. Static only (`sygnal-check`, for literal declarations); the editor offers the rename as a quick fix.
Fix: Rename the key to the one suggested. The keys: a catalog `parts`, `containers`, `description`, `categories`, `rows`, `guidance`, `limits`, `examples`; a part `component`, `render`, `props`, `description`, `state`, `local`, `params`, `in`, `group`, `maxUses`, `required`, `pin`, `companions`, `category`, `result`; a container `slots`, `minSlots`, `min`, `max`, `maxUses`, `accepts`, `arranged`, `direction`, `description`, `in`, `params`, `render`; a param `options`, `default`, `label`, `ask`, `type`, `min`, `max`, `bins`, `maxLength`, `required`, `items`, `from`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG253

## SYG254

SYG254 (info): Catalog descriptions or options overlap
A model composing from a catalog (sygnal/ai `compose.decisions()` or `compose.llm()`) sees a part only as its `description`, and a param only as its options' descriptions. In the evals most selection errors came from three wordings, which this lint flags: two part descriptions that share a phrase (two adjacent content words: "monthly revenue" on both the revenue KPI and the revenue chart pulled in the wrong part); a part description that names one of its own param values ("revenue over the last 12 months" on a part with a `range` param: the description is read for every value);
Fix: Write each description as "Noun (what it shows)", leading with the word a user says for that part and not repeating another part's content ("Revenue (KPI card: this month's total)", "Revenue chart (line chart of the revenue trend)"); put alternatives in a `group`; leave param values out of the description (the param supplies them); word each param's options so they name only what that param changes.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG254

## SYG256

SYG256 (warn): Output guard rejects the updated state
Since Sygnal 7, STATE runs first in a model entry and every other sink gets the committed state. On an installed Sygnal 7 or later, this check reports a STATE write of a literal field value that makes a same-action output guard return the imported ABORT value. For example, STATE sets status to 'working', then HTTP checks state.status !== 'working' and suppresses the request that just started. This conservative check covers simple field comparisons and boolean guards, retaining STATE branch conditions so a guard already known to reject before STATE is not reported.
Fix: Keep the admission guard, but read props.previousState (the state from before the action) for the value that admitted it, for example HTTP: (state, data, next, { previousState }) => previousState.status !== 'working' ? { url: '/work', requestId: state.requestId, ok: 'DONE' } : ABORT. Use the updated state for payload fields written by STATE. Do not remove the guard: STATE returning ABORT does not cancel other sinks, so an unconditional output can send duplicate requests. No automatic fix is offered.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG256

## SYG257

SYG257 (info): Output reads a field its action changed (7.0 timing audit)
An opt-in migration audit for the 7.0 reducer timing: an output sink (EFFECT, HTTP, EVENTS, PARENT, ELEMENT, another driver or a behavior output) read a top-level state field that the same action's STATE changed. Since 7.0 the output gets the new, committed value; in 6.x it got the old one. Reported once per component, action, sink and field.
Fix: If the output meant the value from before the action (an admission guard, a 'was' value), read it from the fourth argument: (state, data, next, { previousState }) => previousState.status ... Otherwise nothing needs to change: the output now sees what STATE wrote.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG257

## SYG258

SYG258 (warn): Clock or randomness read from a global in a STATE reducer
A STATE reducer calls `Date.now()`, `new Date()` with no arguments, `Math.random()` or `crypto.randomUUID()` (also through `globalThis.`, `window.` or `self.`) directly in its body. The reducer then gives a different state each time the same action runs, so replaying recorded actions (record/replay, a test with `renderComponent`) does not reproduce the state. Model handlers receive `now()`, `random()` and `uuid()` on their 4th argument (props); record/replay and `renderComponent` (fixed clock, seeded random, deterministic ids) supply them, so the reducer stays deterministic. Calls in nested functions, views and intents are not reported.
Fix: Take the value from the reducer's 4th argument: `ADD_TASK: (state, title, next, { now, uuid }) => ({ ...state, tasks: [...state.tasks, { id: uuid(), title, created: now() }] })` instead of `crypto.randomUUID()` and `Date.now()`; `new Date()` becomes `new Date(now())`. A component prop with the same name shadows them.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG258

## SYG259

SYG259 (warn): An output reads a field its action's STATE cleared
An action's STATE reducer sets a top-level state field to an empty literal (`''`, `null`, `undefined`, `false`, `[]` or `{}`), and another handler of the same model entry (EFFECT, PARENT, HTTP, EVENTS, ELEMENT or another sink) reads that field from its state argument. Since Sygnal 7.0 the STATE reducer runs first and the other outputs get the committed state, so the handler always reads the cleared value: an Enter that clears a text box and sends its text up with PARENT sends `''`.
Fix: Read the value from before the action, on the handler's 4th argument: `PARENT: (state, data, next, { previousState }) => previousState.text`. Or pass the value in the action's data from the intent (`KEY: DOM.keydown('.box').filter(e => e.key === 'Enter').map(e => e.target.value)`) and read `data`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG259

## SYG260

SYG260 (warn): undo() or undoable() on a key shared() syncs
`shared()` from `sygnal/yjs` keeps `state[key]` in a Yjs document that other clients edit too. Sygnal's `undo({ key })` behavior and `undoable(model, { key })` record snapshots of the whole slice and restore one on UNDO: the restored snapshot is then written to the document like any local edit, so it reverts every change other users made since that snapshot, not only this user's. The Yjs driver has a per-user undo instead: a `Y.UndoManager` per shared key that tracks only this client's own transactions, so a remote change made after this user's edit survives the undo.
Fix: Remove the snapshot undo for that key and send the commands to the driver: `UNDO: { SHARED: { undo: 'board' } }`, `REDO: { SHARED: { redo: 'board' } }`; `shared({ history: 'history' })` puts `{ canUndo, canRedo }` in `state.history` for the buttons. `undo()` on keys that aren't shared keeps working next to it.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG260

## SYG261

SYG261 (warn): shared() inferred the kind of an empty array
Without a `shape`, `shared()` infers how each field of the slice is stored in the Yjs document from its value: an array of objects that all have an `id` becomes an id-keyed collection (concurrent adds, edits, moves and removes of different items merge), any other array a `Y.Array` of plain values. An empty array fits both, so the driver guesses a collection; if the field later holds plain values (strings, numbers), it is switched to a list then, and a concurrent edit by another client can be lost in the switch. Reported once per field path, in dev, when the slice is first written to the document.
Fix: Declare the field's kind: `shared({ shape: { tags: 'list' } })` for plain values, `shared({ shape: { items: collection() } })` (from `sygnal/yjs`) for items with an `id`. Fields the shape leaves out are still inferred.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG261

## SYG262

SYG262 (warn): Canvas data layer rebuilt with equal nodes
A `<shapes items={…}>` data layer of `sygnal/canvas` got a new array in which at least half of its nodes (64 or more) are new objects with exactly the fields of the nodes they replace: a reducer rebuilt every shape (`shapes.map(s => ({ ...s }))`, a JSON round trip, a fresh copy from a store) while changing few or none. The canvas keys its static layer, its translation blits and its camera cache on node identity (as `sygnal/yjs` keys its diff on it), so a layer whose nodes all change identity repaints everything on every frame, silently: the app still works, at a full repaint's cost.
Fix: Replace only the nodes that change and keep the others: `shapes.map(s => s.id === id ? { ...s, x } : s)`, or patch by index. For a selection, look the ids up in a `Set` and return the untouched objects as they are.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG262

## SYG301

SYG301 (error): RxJS operator used on an xstream stream
An RxJS operator such as `pipe`, `switchMap`, `debounceTime` or `tap` was called on a Sygnal stream, which is an xstream stream and does not have it. With `sygnal/diagnostics` loaded, these names are defined on xstream's `Stream.prototype` to throw a `TypeError` that names the xstream equivalent, instead of the bare `x.switchMap is not a function`. A side effect of the dev entry is that `typeof stream.pipe === 'function'` is true while it is loaded.
Fix: Use the xstream equivalent from the message, e.g. `.map(x => inner$).flatten()` for `switchMap`, or `.compose(debounce(ms))` for `debounceTime`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG301

## SYG302

SYG302 (info): Default import from 'xstream' or 'xstream/extra/*'
xstream is published as CommonJS with an `exports.default`, and so is each of its extras (`xstream/extra/dropRepeats`, `debounce`, ...). Bundlers that apply interop give `import xs from 'xstream'` the stream factory, but Node's ESM loader and Vite 8 (in a package with `"type": "module"`) give the module object, so `xs.create`, `xs.merge` and `xs.of` are undefined there, `dropRepeats()` is "not a function", and a driver, intent or test fails when it runs, after `tsc` and the checker passed.
Fix: Import it from Sygnal: `import { xs } from 'sygnal'` (`import { xs as stream } from 'sygnal'` for another name), `import { dropRepeats, debounce } from 'sygnal'`. `sygnal-check --fix` rewrites an import whose only specifier is the default one. For an extra Sygnal doesn't export, resolve the default yourself: `import pairwiseModule from 'xstream/extra/pairwise'` then `const pairwise = pairwiseModule.default ?? pairwiseModule`. To react to a state change, `STATE.watch(fn)` needs no extra at all (SYG303). Types stay importable from xstream: `import type { Stream } from 'xstream'`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG302

## SYG303

SYG303 (info): STATE.stream with dropRepeats() in an intent
An intent builds an action from `STATE.stream` composed with `dropRepeats()`, as in `CHANGED: STATE.stream.map(s => s.tab).compose(dropRepeats())`: the hand-written way to act when part of the state changes. `STATE.watch(fn)` is the canonical form: it emits the selected value each time it changes, compares values structurally (a new array with the same items is no change), works the same in a Collection item (its own state), and needs no xstream extra (a default import of one fails at run time under Node ESM and Vite 8, SYG302).
Fix: Use `STATE.watch(fn)`: `CHANGED: STATE.watch(state => state.tab)`, followed by the same operators (`STATE.watch(s => s.text).compose(debounce(1000))`). Add `{ immediate: true }` (`STATE.watch(fn, { immediate: true })`) when the action must also fire for the current value, as `STATE.stream` did.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG303

## SYG401

SYG401 (warn): Collection 'from' field is missing or not an array
A `<Collection>` needs an array to render. The runtime reports this when `from="field"` names a key that is not in the parent state (or its calculated fields), when that field is not an array, or when a `from={{ get, set }}` getter returns a non-array; the dev entry also reports a `<Collection>` with no `from` whose parent state is not an array. In every case the Collection renders no items: a missing `from` key until the key appears in the state (it then renders, since 6.0), a non-array value until it becomes an array.
Fix: Point `from` at an array field and initialize it in `initialState`, e.g. `initialState = { items: [] }` with `<Collection of={Item} from="items" />`, or make a custom `get()` return an array.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG401

## SYG402

SYG402 (error): Context is not an object
The component's `.context` is set to something other than a plain object (for example a function or an array). It is logged and ignored: the component contributes no context values, and descendants only receive the context inherited from further up. It is logged, not thrown, so rendering continues.
Fix: Define context as an object of named entries: `Comp.context = { theme: state => state.theme }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG402

## SYG403

SYG403 (error): Invalid context entry
A `.context` entry value is not a function. Context entries are functions of state only: the state-key string (`{ user: 'currentUser' }`) and `true` entries Sygnal accepted before 6.0 were removed. That entry is skipped each time context is computed, so descendants read `undefined` for it; the other entries still work. It is logged, not thrown.
Fix: Write each entry as a function of state: `{ user: state => state.currentUser }`. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#leftovers.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG403

## SYG404

SYG404 (error): Context stream errored
The stream that computes a component's context emitted an error, most often because a context function threw. An errored xstream stream stops, so this component's context stops updating for its descendants from that point on. The original error is attached to the log.
Fix: Check the attached error and make each context function safe for every state it can receive (e.g. guard against missing fields with `state.user?.name`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG404

## SYG405

SYG405 (error): Sub-component has initialState without isolatedState
A sub-component defines `initialState` but not `isolatedState = true`, so its `initialState` would overwrite the state slice its parent passes in. For a component rendered by tag in a parent's view this is an error: it is thrown when the child is instantiated, and the parent catches it, logs it under this code and renders its error fallback instead of the child. For Collection items and Switchable children it is only a warning and the initial state still replaces what the parent passed. It doesn't matter whether the tag has a `state` prop: `<Stopwatch state="stopwatch" />` and `<Stopwatch />` both throw.
Fix: Remove `initialState` from the sub-component and let the parent own the state: put the child's start values in the parent's `initialState`, under the field the `state` prop names (`App.initialState = { stopwatch: { ms: 0 } }` for `<Stopwatch state="stopwatch" />`). Or set `Child.isolatedState = true` if the child should keep its own local state.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG405

## SYG406

SYG406 (error): View threw
The component's view function threw while rendering. The error is logged and the component renders its `onError` fallback if it has one, or an empty `<div data-sygnal-error>` otherwise. The app keeps running, but that component shows no real content until a later render succeeds.
Fix: Fix the error in the view (often a missing field on `state` or `props`), and add `Comp.onError = (error, { componentName }) => <div>…</div>` if you want a custom fallback.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG406

## SYG407

SYG407 (error): onError handler threw
A component's `onError` handler threw while handling a view error (SYG406) or a sub-component instantiation error (SYG408). Sygnal logs the second error and renders an empty `<div data-sygnal-error>` instead of your fallback.
Fix: Keep `onError` simple and make it always return a vnode, e.g. `Comp.onError = () => <div class="error">Something went wrong</div>`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG407

## SYG408

SYG408 (error): Sub-component failed to instantiate
Creating a sub-component (a custom component, Collection, or Switchable found in the parent's view) threw an uncoded exception, for example from the child's intent. The parent catches it, logs it with the original error attached, and renders its own `onError` fallback, or an empty `<div data-sygnal-error>`, in that child's place. The rest of the parent keeps rendering. A coded Sygnal error thrown while instantiating (SYG405, SYG413, SYG414, SYG903, ...) is reported under its own code instead, with the same fallback.
Fix: Read the attached error and fix its cause.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG408

## SYG409

SYG409 (warn): Child tried to update a calculated field
A sub-component, Switchable, or Collection is bound to a parent state field (via its `state` or `from` prop) that is one of the parent's `calculated` fields, and the child wrote a new value back to it. Calculated fields are derived from other state, so the write is ignored and the parent state is left unchanged.
Fix: Bind the child to a plain (non-calculated) state field, and change the fields the calculated value is derived from instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG409

## SYG410

SYG410 (error): Invalid sub-component 'state' prop
The `state` prop on a sub-component or Switchable is neither a state key string nor an object with a `get()` function (for example a number, or a `{ set }` object without `get`). It is logged and the child falls back to receiving the parent's whole state, which is usually not what was intended. Also reported (by the dev checks at run time, and by sygnal-check for a literal) when a child's `state` is an empty string, `state=""`, or a path with an empty segment (`"user."`, `".user"`, `"a..b"`): that names an empty key, so the child reads `state[""]`, gets no state and is left out of the view without any other error.
Fix: Pass a state key string (`state="user"`) or a lens object `state={{ get: s => s.user, set: (s, user) => ({ ...s, user }) }}`. For an empty `state`, leave the prop out to share the parent's state (`<Child />`; `sygnal-check --fix` removes `state=""`), or name a key in every segment of the path.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG410

## SYG411

SYG411 (error): Collection 'of' is missing or not a component
A `<Collection>` has no `of` prop, or `of` is not a component function (a component name as a string, `<Collection of="Row">`, is a form Sygnal 6.0 removed; it is also reported as SYG612). This is thrown while the parent's view is processed, so the Collection cannot render.
Fix: Pass the item component function itself: `<Collection of={TaskCard} from="tasks" />`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG411

## SYG412

SYG412 (error): Invalid Collection 'from' prop
The `from` prop on a `<Collection>` is neither a state key string nor an object with a `get()` function. It is logged (not thrown) and the Collection renders nothing.
Fix: Use a state key string (`from="items"`) or a lens object with `get` and `set`: `from={{ get: s => s.items, set: (s, items) => ({ ...s, items }) }}`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG412

## SYG413

SYG413 (error): Retired in 6.0: Unnamed component factory not found
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. Before 6.0 it was logged when a view rendered an element carrying neither a component factory nor its options (`sygnal-factory`). Since 6.0 a component vnode carries the component function itself (`data.c`); there are no factories or options objects to lose.
Fix: Nothing to change. Render components as JSX tags of their functions.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG413

## SYG414

SYG414 (error): Retired in 6.0: Component not found
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. Before 6.0 it was logged when a view rendered a component by a string name that no `.components` registry entry matched. Sygnal 6.0 removed string tags and `.components`: a component is always referenced by its function. A leftover string tag renders as a plain element and is reported as SYG612 in development.
Fix: Import the component and use it as a JSX tag. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#string-tags.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG414

## SYG415

SYG415 (error): Switchable 'of' is missing or invalid
A `<Switchable>` has no `of` prop, `of` is not a plain object, or one of its values is not a component function. This is thrown while the parent's view is processed, so the Switchable cannot render.
Fix: Pass an object mapping names to components: `<Switchable of={{ list: ListView, grid: GridView }} current={state.mode} />`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG415

## SYG416

SYG416 (error): Switchable 'current' is missing or invalid
A `<Switchable>` has no `current` prop, `current` is not a string or function, or `current` is not one of the keys of `of`. This is thrown while the parent's view is processed, so no component can be shown.
Fix: Set `current` to one of the keys of `of`, e.g. `current="list"` when `of={{ list: ListView, grid: GridView }}`, and make sure the state value it comes from is initialized.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG416

## SYG417

SYG417 (warn): Portal target not found
A `<Portal target="…">` selector matched no element in the document. Sygnal retries for a short time (about 10 attempts, 5 ms apart) in case the target is rendered by a sub-component that has not settled yet, then warns and leaves the portal content unrendered.
Fix: Make sure an element matching the `target` selector exists in the page (for example `<div id="modal-root">` in your HTML) before the Portal mounts.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG417

## SYG418

SYG418 (error): Invalid Collection sort prop
The `sort` prop on a `<Collection>` has an unsupported shape: an object with more than one key, a direction that is not `'asc'`, `'desc'`, `1` or `-1`, or a value that is not a string, array, object or function. The invalid sort (or array element) is logged and ignored, so the items are not sorted as intended.
Fix: Use a field name (`sort="title"`), a single-key object (`sort={{ title: 'desc' }}`), a comparator function, or an array of these.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG418

## SYG419

SYG419 (error): Retired in 6.0: Invalid switchable() 'name$' parameter
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was thrown by the low-level `switchable()` helper, which Sygnal 6.0 removed together with the `component()` factory. `<Switchable of={...} current={...} />` is the one form.
Fix: Render `<Switchable of={{ a: A, b: B }} current={state.tab} />` in a view.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG419

## SYG420

SYG420 (error): JSX tag is undefined
A JSX element's tag evaluated to `undefined`, usually because a component was not imported, was misspelled, or was imported as default instead of named (or vice versa). Sygnal renders an `<UNDEFINED>` element in its place and logs the message with `console.error`; it is collected like other runtime diagnostics (the JSX runtime reports it through the diagnostics core, or only prints it when no Sygnal core is loaded).
Fix: Import or define the component in the file that uses it, and check that the import style (default vs named) matches the export.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG420

## SYG421

SYG421 (error): Invalid data (dataset) key
A view renders a `data` key the DOM can't store. `data={{ ... }}` is written with `element.dataset[key] = value`, and the browser throws a SyntaxError DOMException for a key with a hyphen followed by a lower-case letter (`'task-id'`), or an attribute-name error for characters such as spaces, quotes or `=`. The patch fails, so rendering can stop, and the console shows only a bare `DOMException {}`. The dev entry checks every rendered dataset key before the patch and names the key; renderComponent's mock DOM never throws, so it is also the only signal there.
Fix: Use a camelCase key in the `data` prop: `data={{ taskId: 7 }}` renders `data-task-id="7"` (a `data-task-id="7"` JSX attribute works too); read it with `.data('taskId')`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG421

## SYG422

SYG422 (error): Invalid timer spec
A component's `timers` static declares a timer that `makeTimerDriver()` can't run, so it is not started (the other timers are). A spec is `{ every: ms, action }` (a positive interval), `{ after: ms, action }` (0 or more) or `{ frame: 'ACTION' }`, each with an optional `background: true`. Reported for a non-positive or non-numeric `every`, a negative `after`, both `every` and `after`, a missing or non-string `action`, or a `frame` that isn't an action name. A falsy entry (`state.running && { ... }`) is not an error: it means the timer is stopped. sygnal-check reports it too, for specs written as literals (`{ every: 0, action: 'TICK' }`);
Fix: Use `tick: state.running && { every: 100, action: 'TICK' }`, `done: state.armed && { after: 5000, action: 'EXPIRE' }` or `frame: state.animating && { frame: 'FRAME' }`. To stop a timer, return a falsy value for it instead of an invalid spec.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG422

## SYG423

SYG423 (warn): Context change skipped a view whose output it changes
A component reads context, the context changed, and Sygnal did not re-render the component, because its view read none of the changed keys during its last call. Sygnal 6.0 re-renders a component on a context change only when its view read a key that changed. With `sygnal/diagnostics` loaded, a sample of the skipped views is called again with the new context; when the result differs, the page shows a stale render and this is reported.
Fix: Read the entries in the view itself, `context.theme` or `function C({ context: { theme } })`, on every call. Pass a value you need later as a prop or keep it in state instead of a saved context object.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG423

## SYG424

SYG424 (warn): Duplicate Collection item id
Two or more items in a `<Collection>`'s array have the same `id`. A Collection keys its items by `id` (an item without one by its index in the array), so only the first item with that id renders, and the item component's writes go to that first item. The others are not shown.
Fix: Give every item a unique `id` when it is created, for example from a counter in state or `uuid()` from the reducer's 4th argument (`(state, data, next, { uuid }) => …`). Items with no `id` at all are keyed by their index.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG424

## SYG425

SYG425 (warn): isolatedState slice lacks initialState keys
An `isolatedState` component is bound to a slice of its parent's state (`state="key"` or a lens) that already exists, so it keeps that slice and its `initialState` is not applied (since 6.0 the parent's data wins). The slice lacks keys that `initialState` defines, so the component's view and reducers see them as undefined.
Fix: Add `resetState` to the tag (`<Panel state="panel" resetState />`) to start the component from its `initialState`, replacing the slice. To keep the parent's data, initialize the missing keys in the parent's state.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG425

## SYG426

SYG426 (warn): Deprecated lowercase marker tag
A view writes a Sygnal marker as a lowercase string tag: `<collection>` or `<switchable>` (which work without an import), or `<clientonly>`, `<portal>`, `<transition>` or `<suspense>`. The lowercase tags are deprecated since 6.3.0 and will be removed in the next major: the tag will then render an unknown HTML element (`<collection>`) instead of the component, and the Collection and Switchable handlers will load only when their imported components are used. Since 6.3.0 `<portal>`, `<transition>` and `<suspense>` already work only when the capitalized component is used somewhere else in the app.
Fix: Import the component and write it capitalized: `import { Collection } from 'sygnal'` and `<Collection of={Item} from="items" />` (`Switchable`, `Portal`, `Transition` and `Suspense` from 'sygnal', `ClientOnly` from 'sygnal/vike'). `sygnal-check --fix` renames the tags and adds the import.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG426

## SYG427

SYG427 (error): CHILD.select() of something that is not a component
A component is imported from a module that doesn't export it, so the binding is `undefined`. The browser refuses to load the module ("does not provide an export named …"), but Vitest runs on with `undefined`: `CHILD.select(Child)` never emits, and `<Child />` renders nothing (SYG420, only when that branch renders). A test that never shows the branch passes, with no diagnostic. With `sygnal/diagnostics` loaded, `CHILD.select()` of anything but a function is reported when the component is created, so every test of the parent catches it.
Fix: Export the component from its module (`export function Child() { … }`), or fix the imported name. Pass `CHILD.select()` the component function itself.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG427

## SYG428

SYG428 (warn): A state path that names a key containing a dot
Since 6.5.0, a child's `state="a.b"`, a Switchable's `state` and a Collection's `from="a.b"` are paths: `state.a.b` (`a[0].b` for an array position). Before, the string was one key, so a state with a key that itself contains a dot (`{ 'a.b': [...] }`) was read directly. Such a key is now missed: the designator reads `state.a.b`, which is undefined, so the child or the Collection renders nothing, and the first write creates `{ a: { b: ... } }` beside the old key. The dev diagnostics report it when the owner's state has a key equal to the designator.
Fix: Rename the key so it has no dot (`{ ab: [...] }` with `state="ab"`), or keep it and pass a lens: `state={{ get: (s) => s['a.b'], set: (s, v) => ({ ...s, 'a.b': v }) }}`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG428

## SYG429

SYG429 (warn): Switchable state map names no page
A Switchable's `state` can be a map from page names to bindings, `state={{ projects: 'pages.projects', settings: 'pages.settings' }}`: each listed page binds its own slice (a key, a path, a lens or a `byId` selection) with a tag child's lifetime rules, and the pages not listed share the owner's state. A key that is not one of the `of` pages binds nothing, so the page it was meant for (usually a typo of its name) shares the owner's whole state instead of its slice. The dev checks report it once per component and key when the Switchable renders; `sygnal-check` reports it when `of` is an object literal.
Fix: Use the page's name from `of={{ … }}` as the key (the message names the closest one), or remove the entry.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG429

## SYG430

SYG430 (warn): VirtualCollection has no bounded height
A `<VirtualCollection>` is its own scroll container (`overflow-y: auto`) and renders the rows that fit in its height. Its element is either 0 px tall, so no row is in view, or as tall as all of its rows (its height comes from its content, e.g. no `height` in its class, or a `max-height: 100%`, `calc()` of a percentage or `fit-content` that resolves against a parent without a height; Sygnal measures whether the height follows the rows), so it never scrolls and would render every row. In the second case Sygnal renders only the rows within the viewport's height, and rows further down the page stay empty.
Fix: Give its `className` a bounded height: `.rows { height: 400px }` or `max-height`, or in a flex column `flex: 1; min-height: 0`. Check that a parent with `display: none` isn't the cause of a 0 height.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG430

## SYG431

SYG431 (warn): VirtualCollection items without ids
Items of a `<VirtualCollection>`'s array have no `id`, so they are keyed by their index (as in a Collection, D169). A VirtualCollection keeps a measured height and an instance per key: when items are added, removed or reordered, both follow the position, not the item, so rows get each other's heights and a row's instance shows another item. Reported once per VirtualCollection.
Fix: Give every item a unique `id`, e.g. `rows: data.map((r) => ({ id: r.key, ...r }))`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG431

## SYG432

SYG432 (warn): VirtualCollection item does not render one element
The item component of a `<VirtualCollection>` rendered a fragment (an array of elements) or text. A VirtualCollection measures each row's root element and sets `data-index`, `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` on it; a fragment has no root element, so its rows can't be measured (later rows overlap or leave gaps) or announced in position. Reported once per VirtualCollection.
Fix: Return one element from the item's view: wrap its content in a `<div>` (or an `<li>`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG432

## SYG433

SYG433 (warn): VirtualCollection scroll target not in the list
An element command `{ scrollToIndex: target, index }` or `{ scrollToId: target, id }` reached a `<VirtualCollection>` with an index outside its rows (an index counts the rows after `filter` and `sort`, from 0) or an id that no shown item has (not in the array, or filtered out). It didn't scroll.
Fix: Send an integer index from 0 to the number of shown rows minus 1, or the id of an item the filter keeps: `{ scrollToId: '.rows', id: row.id }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG433

## SYG434

SYG434 (warn): Invalid VirtualCollection estimateSize or overscan
`estimateSize` must be a positive number (a row's height in px before it is measured) or a function `(item, index) => px`, and `overscan` a number ≥ 0 (rows rendered beyond each edge). Another value is ignored: 32 px and 5 rows are used instead.
Fix: Pass `estimateSize={32}` (about your row height) or `(item) => (item.expanded ? 120 : 32)`, and `overscan={5}`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG434

## SYG435

SYG435 (warn): Sortable list shown filtered or in another order
`sortable` moves entries of `state[from]`: the arrow keys swap the item with its neighbour in the array, Home / End move it to the array's ends, the announced positions count the array, and a pointer drop lands next to the entry it is dropped on. When the list is rendered from a `<Collection>` with `sort` (or `filter` that hides entries between shown ones), the shown order isn't the array's: under a sort a move changes nothing visible (the Collection sorts it back), and under a filter a keyboard step can pass hidden entries and the positions count entries nobody sees.
Fix: Reorder only a list that is shown as it is stored: drop the Collection's `sort` for a reorderable list (sort the array itself, once, if it needs an initial order), and while a filter hides entries hide the drag handles (or render the full list) so a move can't pass hidden ones.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG435

## SYG436

SYG436 (warn): VirtualCollection estimateSize far from the measured row heights
`<VirtualCollection estimateSize={n}>` counts every row that hasn't been rendered yet as `n` px tall; a rendered row is measured. When the real rows are taller than the estimate, the list's total height is too short until the rows near the end have been rendered and measured, so a fast scroll to the end shows blank space where the last rows belong and the scrollbar jumps as the total grows; when they are much shorter, the scrollbar shrinks and jumps instead. The dev entry compares a numeric `estimateSize` with the median of the first 10 measured rows and reports it once per list when they differ by more than 1.3×.
Fix: Pass the rows' real height, `estimateSize={71}` (the message gives the measured median); when unsure, err high. When rows differ predictably, pass a function: `estimateSize={(item) => (item.image ? 240 : 56)}`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG436

## SYG440

SYG440 (warn): Two agent declarations with the same name
Agent tools are named after the declaration (`agent.name`, else the component name): `todos_read`, `todos_add`. Two shown instances with different declarations, or the same non-item component rendered twice, produce the same tool names, so only the first one's tools are offered and the other can't be reached. (Collection items of one component are one keyed tool and are not reported.) Reported once per name while an agent layer runs. sygnal-check reports two declarations with the same literal name (or none, so the component names collide) when one component renders both, directly or through its children.
Fix: Give each declaration its own `agent.name` (for a component rendered twice, derive it from a prop: `Panel.agent = { name: 'left_panel', ... }` on a wrapper per place), or narrow the layer with `agentTools(app, { from })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG440

## SYG441

SYG441 (warn): Agent Collection items without unique ids
A Collection item component's `agent` actions become one tool with an `id` parameter whose values are the items' ids. Items without an `id` are keyed by their index, which shifts when an item is added or removed, so a model's call can reach the wrong item. Items whose ids repeat across Collections of the same item component (the same card id in two board lanes) are ambiguous: the call reaches the first. Reported once per declaration while an agent layer runs.
Fix: Give every item an `id` that is unique across all the Collections of that item component (`{ id: 'todo-1', ... }`), or add an owner-level action that takes the qualified key (`MOVE_CARD: { input: z.object({ lane, card }) }`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG441

## SYG442

SYG442 (error): Chat or command bar behavior not connected to its app
The `chat` and `commandBar` behaviors (sygnal/ai) run agent actions through the app's runtime, which they reach through a hook layer every app picks up when it starts. The first `chat()` or `commandBar()` call installs that layer, and also adds it to the app already running that `run()` registered (the page's first live app), so a component using one of them loaded lazily into that app works. Another app started before the first call (a second `run()` on the page, a `sygnal/element` custom element) can't be found and has none: its assistant still streams replies, but sends no tools, no `read` context, and runs no tool calls;
Fix: Make the first `chat()` / `commandBar()` call happen before `run()`: define the host component (or call the factory once) in a module the entry imports, not only in a component loaded later.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG442

## SYG450

SYG450 (warn): Catalog in names an unknown container or slot
A part's (or container's) `in` lists the places it may go, as `'container'` (any of its slots) or `'container:slot'`; the root is `'page'`. An entry names a container the catalog doesn't declare, a slot that container doesn't have, or the built-in `row` (rows are transparent: a part in a row is where the row is). That entry is ignored; with none left the part goes on the page. The same code reports a container's `min` / `max` that isn't a non-negative integer, `min` above `max`, a `maxUses` that isn't a positive integer, or `accepts` other than `'leaves'` (ignored). Reported in development, when the catalog is defined;
Fix: Name declared containers and slots (`in: ['page', 'tabs:billing']`), and declare the container in `containers` before using it in `in`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG450

## SYG451

SYG451 (warn): Composed has no catalog or from is not a composition
`<Composed catalog={catalog} from="page" />` (sygnal/ai) renders the composition kept at `from` in the host component's state, with the catalog's parts. Here it can't: the `catalog` prop is missing (or isn't made by `defineCatalog()`), the value at `from` (a key, default `'page'`, or a path such as `['boards', 0, 'page']`) is not a composition (an object with a `layout`, as the `compose` behavior keeps under its key in `uses`), or `card` is not an `ask_user` tool part. The marker renders nothing and the rest of the view goes on.
Fix: Pass the catalog and the key of the compose behavior in `uses`: `App.uses = { page: compose(catalog, { backend }) }` with `<Composed catalog={catalog} from="page" />`. For a composition the view computes, call `catalog.render(slice, state)` in the view instead. For a chat card, pass the tool part: `<Composed catalog={catalog} card={part} />`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG451

## SYG452

SYG452 (warn): Layout lists a node key twice
A layout's node keys are identities: each node appears in exactly one slot, once. This layout lists a key in two places (or inside itself, a cycle). A key is the identity of a part's instance, so two places can't share it. The first place (in depth-first order) is kept and the others are dropped. It comes from a hand-made layout passed to `SET_LAYOUT` or from editing `nodes` directly. Reported in development, by the finishing step.
Fix: Give each node its own key (a repeat of a part is `part~2`), and move a node by removing its key from the old slot. `fromTree(catalog, tree, previous)` builds keys for you.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG452

## SYG453

SYG453 (warn): Two children with the same identity share one instance
A component instance's identity among its parent view's children is its component plus its `key`, else its `id` prop, else its position in the view. Two tags of the same component with the same `key` (or `id`) in one view, anywhere in it, are the same identity, so they are one instance: it has one state, both places show its output, and the second tag's props replace the first's. Reported once per parent, component and key.
Fix: Give each tag a key that is unique among its parent view's children, usually from the data it shows (`<Card key={card.id} />`). Use the same key for the same thing on every render: a new key makes a new instance.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG453

## SYG454

SYG454 (warn): State binding changed without a new component identity
In Sygnal 6 a retained component's state path or byId binding is fixed at mount. A changing byId selector without a corresponding key can keep reading and writing the old record. Sygnal 7 disposes and remounts components when a known state path or byId target changes, even with the same explicit key; equivalent fresh byId objects preserve the component. Opaque custom lenses remain mount-bound. The static checker reports direct dynamic unkeyed byId selections only when the installed Sygnal is known to be 6; it is silent for 7 and when the installed version cannot be determined (no node_modules, Yarn PnP, git-tree --base checks).
Fix: On Sygnal 6 write <Workspace key={selected.id} state={byId('projects', selected.id)} />. The key creates a new component lifetime, disposing the old requests, timers and subscriptions. On Sygnal 7 known paths and byId targets remount automatically. For an opaque custom lens whose target changes, use an explicit key; memoization or forcing a render cannot identify its semantic target.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG454

## SYG455

SYG455 (error): Outlet from names no wizard behavior
`<Outlet from="wizard">` renders the current step of the `wizard()` behavior the component declares under that key in its `uses`. The key names none (a typo, or `uses` declares the wizard under another key, or on another component), so the outlet has no steps to show and renders nothing. The runtime reports it once per component, in production too; the static checker reports it for a string `from` when the component's `uses` can be read, and also when the key names a behavior that isn't `wizard()`.
Fix: Declare the behavior on the component that renders the outlet, under the key `from` names: `NewFilter.uses = { wizard: wizard({ steps }) }` with `<Outlet of={STEPS} from="wizard" />`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG455

## SYG456

SYG456 (error): Outlet has no component for the current name
`<Outlet of={…}>` renders `of[name]` for the current name: the wizard's current step (`from`), the route's name (`route`), or `current`. The map has no component under that name, so nothing is rendered in its place. Typical causes: a step added to `wizard({ steps })` but not to `of`, or a route (the not-found route too) with no page. The runtime reports it once per component and name, in production too, when it happens; the static checker reports each step of the wizard's `steps` with no key in an `of` object literal.
Fix: Add the component under that name: `of={{ source: Source, review: Review }}` with one key per step name, or one per route name in route mode (`notFound: NotFound` included).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG456

## SYG457

SYG457 (warn): Outlet of names no step of its wizard
An `<Outlet of={{ … }} from="wizard">` maps step names to components, and one of its keys is not a step of the `wizard()` it names (its `steps` option). That entry never renders: a misspelled step name (its step then has no component, SYG456), or a step that was removed from the flow. Reported when `of` and `steps` are object literals of named keys.
Fix: Rename the key to the step it is for (the checker suggests the closest name), or remove the entry.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG457

## SYG458

SYG458 (warn): Declaration reads a context field off its bag
Since Sygnal 7.2 the second argument of the declaration statics `resources`, `timers`, `connections`, `head`, `browser` and `route` is the bag the view gets, `{ ...props, state, context, uid }`, not the context. For compatibility the context's own fields are still readable on the bag until 8.0, so `Page.resources = { item: (state, { route }) => ... }` keeps working, but 8.0 removes them; and when the component also takes a prop of that name the bag's own key wins, so the declaration reads the prop, not the context field. The dev entry reports the read at run time.
Fix: Read it from the bag's context: `Page.resources = { item: (state, { context: { route } }) => '/api/items/' + route.params.id }` instead of `(state, { route }) => ...`, and `bag.context.route` instead of `bag.route`. `sygnal-check --fix` rewrites the destructuring form, keeping props at the top level: `(state, { id, route })` becomes `(state, { id, context: { route } })`, merged into an existing `context: { ... }` entry. A TypeScript annotation moves with them: `(state, { route }: Ctx)` becomes `(state, { context: { route } }: { context: Ctx })`, and a type literal's members move the same way;
More: sygnal-check explain SYG458

## SYG459

SYG459 (warn): Behavior option reads a state field off its bag
Since Sygnal 7.2 the functions of a behavior's options (the wizard's `when`, `valid`, `label`, `visit`, `dirty`, `discard`, `dialog`, `draft`, `key`, `resetTo`, `url.from`; the form's `values`, `dynamic`, `request`) get the bag the view gets, `{ ...props, state, context, uid }`, after their own arguments. Before 7.2 the wizard's second argument was the host's state, so `when: (step, h) => h.route` still runs but reads `undefined`: the bag has no `route` prop. TypeScript types a behavior bag's props as `unknown`, which catches the reads whose value is used, but not every one.
Fix: Read the host's state from the bag: `when: (step, { state }) => state.route.name === 'review'`, or `h.state.route` instead of `h.route`. `sygnal-check --fix` rewrites `h.route` to `h.state.route`, and `(step, { route })` to `(step, { state: { route } })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG459

## SYG501

SYG501 (error): Removed in 6.0: view with positional arguments
Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). The view declares more than one parameter, as in `function Lane(props, state, context)`. Sygnal 6.0 removed positional view arguments: a view is called with one argument, so `state` and `context` are undefined in the second and third parameters. At run time the dev checks report the same form as SYG612 (`positional-views`).
Fix: Destructure the one argument: `function Lane({ state, context, ...props })`. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#positional-views.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG501

## SYG502

SYG502 (warn): Retired in 6.0: STATE reducer signals no change without ABORT
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. Before 6.0, strict mode flagged a STATE reducer that returned the state object it received (`return state`, `cond ? next : state`) instead of `ABORT`, because that still produced a new state. Since 6.0 returning the identical object is "no change", the same as `ABORT`: no state is emitted and nothing re-renders. A reducer that mutates the state in place and then returns it is reported by SYG222 instead.
Fix: Nothing to change: `return state` and `return ABORT` are equivalent in a STATE reducer. To change the state, return a new object.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG502

## SYG503

SYG503 (warn): Side effect in a STATE reducer that returns ABORT
Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). A STATE reducer runs a call whose result is unused (such as `cmd.send('play')`, `next('X')` or `localStorage.setItem(…)`) and then returns `ABORT`. This is the old pattern for side effects; the canonical form puts side effects in an `EFFECT` sink so STATE reducers stay pure. The check is a heuristic.
Fix: Move the side effect to an EFFECT sink: `PLAY: { EFFECT: (state, data, next) => { cmd.send('play') } }`, keeping any state change in `STATE`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG503

## SYG504

SYG504 (error): Removed in 6.0: 'ACTION | SINK' model key
Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). A model key uses the `'ACTION | SINK'` shorthand, such as `'SEND | EFFECT': …`. Sygnal 6.0 removed these keys: the object form is the only form. `sygnal-check --strict --fix` rewrites the key when no other entry handles the same action. At run time the dev checks report it as SYG612 (`pipe-keys`).
Fix: Use the object form: `SEND: { EFFECT: (state, data, next) => … }`, merging into an existing `SEND` entry if there is one. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#pipe-keys.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG504

## SYG505

SYG505 (warn): Non-canonical EVENTS emit
Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). A model entry emits a global event with `emit('TYPE', fn)` (as the whole entry or spread into the object form), or its EVENTS sink builds the `{ type: 'TYPE', data }` object by hand. The canonical form is an `EVENTS` sink using `event()` inside the object form. `--fix` rewrites the common cases and adds the `event` import.
Fix: Use `ACTION: { EVENTS: event('TYPE', (state, data) => payload) }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG505

## SYG506

SYG506 (error): Removed in 6.0: CHILD.select() with a component name
Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). An intent calls `CHILD.select('TaskCard')` with the child's name as a string. Sygnal 6.0 removed name lookups: children are matched by their component function. `--fix` replaces the string with the identifier when that name is in scope. At run time the dev checks report it as SYG612 (`child-select-name`).
Fix: Pass the component function: `CHILD.select(TaskCard)` (import it first if needed). See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#child-select-name.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG506

## SYG507

SYG507 (info): Prop drilled through more than 2 component levels
Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). A component receives a prop from its parent and passes it on unchanged, under the same name, to its own child component, so the value crosses three component levels. Data that flows that far down belongs in `.context`, which reaches every descendant without each level forwarding it. This is informational only.
Fix: Provide the value as context on the top component, e.g. `Parent.context = { theme: state => state.theme }`, and read `context.theme` where it is needed.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG507

## SYG508

SYG508 (warn): select()/errors() round trip where reply actions would do
Strict mode only. A component sends a request with `category: 'quote'` to a driver with reply actions (`makeFetchDriver`, `driverFromAsync`, or a sink named `HTTP`) and reads the reply back in its own intent with `HTTP.select('quote')` or `HTTP.errors('quote')`. The canonical form is a request with reply actions: it names them in the request, so the intent line, the category string and the select/errors split all go away, and the reply reaches exactly the component instance that sent it. `select()`/`errors()` remain for requests without reply actions and for stream-level composition (see Alternative forms).
Fix: Name the reply actions in the request and remove the intent line: `LOAD: { HTTP: (state) => ({ url: '/api/quote', ok: 'LOADED', error: 'FAILED' }) }`, with `LOADED: (state, body) => …` (the parsed body) and `FAILED: (state, { status }) => …` in the model.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG508

## SYG509

SYG509 (warn): Clock or randomness read from a global in a handler
Strict mode only (`sygnal-check --strict`). A model handler (a STATE reducer, an EFFECT handler, another sink's handler or the payload function of `event()`) calls `Date.now()`, `new Date()` with no arguments, `Math.random()` or `crypto.randomUUID()` (also through `globalThis.`, `window.` or `self.`) directly in its body. The canonical form takes `now()`, `random()` and `uuid()` from the handler's 4th argument (props), which record/replay and `renderComponent` (fixed clock, seeded random, deterministic ids) supply, so replaying the actions gives the same result. Calls in nested functions, views and intents are not reported.
Fix: Use the handler's 4th argument: `SAVE: { EFFECT: (state, data, next, { now }) => { localStorage.setItem('savedAt', String(now())) } }`, or `(state, data, next, props) => … props.uuid() …`; `new Date()` becomes `new Date(now())`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG509

## SYG510

SYG510 (warn): waitForState matched only a state the test had already seen
Strict mode only (`renderComponent(C, { strict: true })` or `configureStrict(true)`). `t.waitForState(pred)` searches the recorded history first, so it resolves at once when any earlier state matches. Reported when the only match is a state from before the test's last awaited input (`await t.simulateEvent(...)`, `await t.simulateAction(...)`) and the current state doesn't match: the wait was true in the past and proves nothing about now. A match the current state also satisfies (`count === 0` again after a reset) isn't reported.
Fix: Assert the current state, `expect(t.state).toMatchObject({ ... })`, or wait for a new state, `await t.next(pred)`. To wait for a state an input will cause, call `t.next(pred)` before the input, or await the input and read `t.state`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG510

## SYG601

SYG601 (error): Retired in 6.0: Missing or invalid sources
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was thrown when a component made by the `component({ ... })` factory was called by hand without a sources object. Sygnal 6.0 removed the factory and its `sources` option; components are always started by `run()` or `renderComponent()`.
Fix: Start the app with `run(App)` (or test it with `renderComponent(App)`). See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#component-factory.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG601

## SYG602

SYG602 (error): Intent is not a function
The component's `.intent` is set but is not a function (for example an object of streams). It is thrown when the component is constructed.
Fix: Make intent a function of sources: `Comp.intent = ({ DOM }) => ({ CLICK: DOM.select('.btn').events('click') })`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG602

## SYG603

SYG603 (error): Intent returned an invalid value
The intent function returned something other than an object of streams: often `undefined` because an arrow function used a block body without `return`, or a single stream of `{ type, data }` objects (a form Sygnal 6.0 removed; the message names it). It is also thrown when an entry of the object is not a stream. It is thrown when the component is constructed.
Fix: Return an object of action streams, e.g. `intent = ({ DOM }) => ({ CLICK: DOM.select('.btn').events('click') })` (note the parentheses around the object).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG603

## SYG604

SYG604 (error): Retired in 6.0: Invalid hmrActions
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was thrown for an `hmrActions` static that was not an action name or an array of them. Sygnal 6.0 removed `hmrActions`: `sygnal/vite` keeps the state across a hot update; a leftover `hmrActions` is reported as SYG612.
Fix: Remove `hmrActions`; put an action to run after the swap in the model's `BOOTSTRAP`. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#hmractions.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG604

## SYG605

SYG605 (error): Retired in 6.0: Intent action name contains '|'
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. `|` was reserved in action names for the `'ACTION | SINK'` model keys, which Sygnal 6.0 removed.
Fix: Nothing to change (a name without `|` stays the clearer choice).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG605

## SYG606

SYG606 (error): calculated is not an object
The component's `.calculated` is set but is not a plain object (for example a function or an array). It is thrown the first time calculated fields are added to an object state.
Fix: Define calculated fields as an object: `Comp.calculated = { total: state => state.items.length }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG606

## SYG607

SYG607 (error): Retired in 6.0: State source not found
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was thrown by the low-level `switchable()` helper when the sources had no state source under its `stateSourceName`. Sygnal 6.0 removed the helper and the custom source names: the state source is always `STATE`.
Fix: Render `<Switchable>` in a view; remove `stateSourceName`. See https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6#source-names.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG607

## SYG608

SYG608 (warn): Strict mode requested without the diagnostics entry
`run(App, drivers, { diagnostics: { strict: true } })` was called but the `sygnal/diagnostics` dev entry is not loaded. The strict (canonical-form) checks live in that entry, so no strict findings are reported; the option still turns diagnostics on. Printed once per page load.
Fix: Import the dev entry before `run()` in development (`import 'sygnal/diagnostics'`), or use the Sygnal Vite plugin, which injects it in dev. Do not ship it in production builds.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG608

## SYG609

SYG609 (warn): Sink or source has no driver
A component's model sends to a sink (for example `HTTP: (state) => ({ url: '/api/x' })`), or its intent reads a source (`HTTP.select('x')`), but `run()` got no driver with that name. Values sent to a sink without a driver are dropped silently, and a source without a driver is `undefined`, so the intent then fails with "Cannot read properties of undefined". `renderComponent()` does not report this: in tests it records such sinks (`t.requests(name)`) and fakes such sources (`t.respond` / `t.fail`), so a test suite can pass while the app drops every request.
Fix: Pass the driver to `run()` under exactly that name: `run(App, { HTTP: makeFetchDriver() })` for HTTP requests, `run(App, { LLM: makeChatDriver({ transport: openResponses({ baseURL, model }) }) })` (from `sygnal/ai`) for an LLM chat sink, `driverFromAsync(fn)` for any promise-returning function, or your own driver. Check the spelling against the drivers you pass.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG609

## SYG610

SYG610 (error): Request has a 'then' or 'catch' key
A request sent to a driver with reply actions (`makeFetchDriver`, `driverFromAsync`) has a `then` or `catch` key, for example `HTTP: (state) => ({ url: '/api/x', then: 'LOADED' })`. An object with a `then` key is a thenable, so it breaks anything that `await`s it, and these keys look like a promise chain but do nothing. The driver does not send the request.
Fix: Name the reply actions with the `ok` / `error` keys: `{ url: '/api/x', ok: 'LOADED', error: 'FAILED' }`. The `ok` action gets the parsed body, the `error` action `{ error, status, body, request }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG610

## SYG611

SYG611 (error): Socket message not sent or connection not opened
A value sent to a `makeSocketDriver()` sink could not be acted on. Either a send (`{ to: 'room', json }`) names a connection that this component instance has not declared, that has closed for good (`reconnect: false`, or a URL the browser rejected), or that is a server-sent events connection, which is read-only. Or a declared connection has neither a `socket` nor an `sse` URL. Or the value is neither `{ connections }` nor `{ to, … }`. Connection names are per component instance: a parent cannot send on a child's connection. The message is dropped; a connection that is only (re)connecting is not an error, its sends are queued.
Fix: Declare the connection first, `{ connections: { room: { socket: '/ws/rooms/general', message: 'RECEIVED' } } }`, then send on it from the same component: `{ to: 'room', json: { text } }`. Use a WebSocket (`socket:`) for two-way traffic.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG611

## SYG612

SYG612 (error): Removed in 6.0
A component uses a form that Sygnal 6.0 removed, so it is ignored or fails at run time: a component named by a string tag or registered in `.components`, `<Collection of="Name">`, the Collection's wrapper element (`className`, `style`, `class`, `attrs`, `data` / `data-*`, `on`, `hook` or `ref` on `<Collection>`: the items now render directly into the parent element, so these went to a `<div>` that no longer exists and are ignored), `CHILD.select('Name')`, an `'ACTION | SINK'` model key, `.peers`, `hmrActions`, a view with positional parameters (`function C(props, state)`), `DOMSourceName` / `stateSourceName`, `storeCalculatedInState`, or the…
Fix: Follow the linked section of the migration guide (https://sygnal.js.org/guide/migrating-to-6): import components and use them as JSX tags, pass the component function to `of` and `CHILD.select`, put a Collection's class or style on your own wrapping element (`<ul className="x"><Collection of={Item} from="items" /></ul>`), use object-form model entries, destructure the view's one argument, and write function components with statics (or use `defineComponent`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG612

## SYG620

SYG620 (error): Router command not performed
A value sent to the router's sink (`makeRouter().driver`) could not be acted on, so nothing was navigated. Either `{ to }` names no route (or the `'*'` not-found route), or the route's pattern needs a param that `params` leaves out, or the value uses the `route` key, which is reserved for the component's `route` declaration (`App.route = 'ROUTE'`), or it is none of the router's commands. The router reports this in production too.
Fix: Navigate with `{ to: 'task', params: { id } }` (plus `query`, `hash`, `replace` as needed), `{ url: router.href(...) }`, `{ back: true }`, `{ forward: true }`, `{ block: 'CONFIRM_LEAVE' }` or `{ prefetch: 'task', params }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG620

## SYG630

SYG630 (warn): Cached request is not idempotent
A request to `makeFetchDriver()` sets `cache: true` or `staleTime` but is not a GET or HEAD (a request with `json` or `body` defaults to POST), for example `{ url: '/api/quotes', method: 'POST', json, cache: true }`. The driver's `queryCache()` keeps its reply by method, URL and body, so a second identical write within `staleTime` is answered from the cache and never reaches the server, and identical writes in flight share one fetch. Writes should always be sent.
Fix: Remove `cache` / `staleTime` from the write. To refresh cached reads after it succeeds, tag the reads (`tags: ['quotes']`) and add `invalidates: ['quotes']` to the write.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG630

## SYG631

SYG631 (error): validate is not a Standard Schema
A request or resource to `makeFetchDriver()` has a `validate` value that is not a Standard Schema, an object with a `~standard.validate` function (zod, valibot and arktype schemas are). A plain function or another validator's object does not qualify. The driver cannot validate the reply, so the request fails with a TypeError on its `error` action (or as the resource's error).
Fix: Pass the schema object itself: `validate: QuoteSchema` (for zod, `z.object({ ... })`). To check a body with your own function, use `parse: (res) => res.json().then(check)` instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG631

## SYG632

SYG632 (info): invalidate matched nothing
A `{ invalidate }` value sent to `makeFetchDriver()` matched no cache entry and no mounted resource, so nothing was refetched or marked stale. Tags are explicit: `{ invalidate: 'quotes' }` matches only requests with `tags: ['quotes']`; a string starting with '/' is a prefix of the request's `url` as written (without the driver's `baseUrl`); a function is called with each request. This is info: invalidating data that no component shows at the moment is often fine.
Fix: Add `tags: ['quotes']` to the resources (or cached requests) the write should refresh, or invalidate by URL prefix: `{ invalidate: '/quotes' }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG632

## SYG633

SYG633 (warn): abort names a lane the requests do not use
`{ abort: 'X' }` cancels this component instance's requests whose key is 'X'; a request's key is its `key`, else its `ok` action, else its `error` action. The instance sends its `ok: 'X'` requests with another `key`, so the abort matches none of them and they still deliver. (G-175.)
Fix: Abort by that key: `{ abort: true, key: 'search' }`, or drop `key` from the requests so their lane is the `ok` action.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG633

## SYG634

SYG634 (info): latest: true with a computed key
A request has `latest: true` and a `key` that is not a string literal, for example `key: 'search-' + state.q`. `latest` cancels this instance's earlier requests with the same key, so a key that changes with state gives every value its own lane, and a new request never cancels the previous one: out-of-order replies can still arrive. That is right for independent lanes, such as one save per row, so this is info.
Fix: Use a fixed key (`key: 'search'`) or none (the lane is the `ok` action) so the newest request cancels the others. Keep a computed key only for lanes that should run side by side (`// sygnal-ignore SYG634`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG634

## SYG635

SYG635 (warn): Caching asked for without a queryCache
A request or resource sets `cache: true` or `staleTime`, or the component sends `{ prefetch: request }`, but the sink's `makeFetchDriver()` has no query cache. The cache is a separate export, so a driver without `cache: queryCache()` caches nothing: the request is sent as an ordinary one, and a prefetch does nothing.
