In tests the HTTP fake has no cache unless `renderComponent(C, { http: { cache: queryCache() } })` gives it one.
Fix: Give the driver a cache: `makeFetchDriver({ cache: queryCache({ staleTime: 30000 }) })` with `import { queryCache } from 'sygnal'` (in tests, `renderComponent(C, { http: { cache: queryCache() } })`). Or remove `cache` / `staleTime` / the prefetch.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG635

## SYG636

SYG636 (warn): progress that can't be reported as asked
A request sets `progress` (a reply action such as `progress: 'UPLOADING'`, or `true` for `HTTP.progress()`), but the driver can't report it as written. A request with `progress` goes over XMLHttpRequest, the only transport that reports upload progress in every browser, and XMLHttpRequest has no equivalent for some fetch options: `init.keepalive`, `priority`, `cache`, `redirect`, `integrity`, `mode`, `referrer`, `referrerPolicy`, `window` and `duplex` are ignored for that request. `progress` on a resource or on a `batch` request is ignored altogether: those report no progress.
Fix: Remove the fetch-only `init` options from the progress request, or drop `progress` if the request needs them. For a resource, send the download as a request with `progress` and reply actions (`{ url, progress: 'DOWNLOADING', ok: 'LOADED', error: 'FAILED' }`); for a batch, send the parts as separate requests.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG636

## SYG637

SYG637 (warn): refresh on a read another component also declares
An action sends `{ refresh: name }` for a resource whose read another component also declares. `refresh` refetches only the sending component's own resources, so the other component keeps showing the old answer until something else refetches it: a header badge stays stale after the page below it refreshes. Nothing fails: the request is sent, the sender updates, and a test of the sender passes. Two reads count as the same when they ask for one literal URL by GET; with a `query`, only when they come from one helper called without arguments.
Fix: Send `{ invalidate: value }` on the HTTP sink instead, with a tag both reads carry or their URL: it refetches every mounted copy. A URL is a prefix, so `'/alerts'` also matches `'/alerts/1'`. If only this component's copy should update, add `// sygnal-ignore SYG637`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG637

## SYG640

SYG640 (warn): Element command target not found
A model entry sent an element command on the built-in `ELEMENT` sink, such as `{ focus: Email }` or `{ showModal: HelpDialog }`, and nothing matched its target. The target, a control or a selector, is looked up only in the view of the component instance that sent the command: an element inside a child component is isolated from its parent, and a Collection item reaches only its own elements. The dev entry's message says when a matching element is on the page but outside the sender's view (rendered by an ancestor, a child component or another part of the page).
Fix: Render the element in the sending component's view, or send the command from the component that renders it: in a Collection, each item sends its own (for example on BOOTSTRAP for a new row). For an element an ancestor renders (a wizard's footer button focusing the page's name field), hand it off: the child emits `EVENTS: event('NAME_FIRST')` (or sends `PARENT`), the ancestor selects it in its intent (`NAME_FIRST: EVENTS.select('NAME_FIRST')`) and its entry sends `ELEMENT: { focus: '#project-name' }`. For an element inside a child, the parent can send `{ focus: focusWithin('.title') }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG640

## SYG641

SYG641 (error): Unknown element command
An element command (`ELEMENT` sink) names a method that can't run. The first key of a command object is the method and the other keys are its options (`{ scrollIntoView: Row, block: 'nearest' }`). A control whose spec object declares `commands` is asked first; then the element's own method runs (focus, blur, select, click, scrollIntoView, showModal, show, close, showPopover, hidePopover, togglePopover, and others such as play or reset). Reported when neither exists, for example a typo (`fokus`) or `showModal` on an element that isn't a `<dialog>`; the message names the control's declared commands.
Fix: Use one of the element's methods or the control's commands, with the method as the first key: `{ focus: Email, preventScroll: true }`, `{ close: HelpDialog, returnValue: 'ok' }`. Render dialogs as `<dialog>` and popovers with `attrs: { popover: 'auto' }`. To change what the page shows, change the state instead.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG641

## SYG642

SYG642 (warn): Persisted state could not be restored or saved
`persist({ ... })` failed to read, migrate or write the stored state: the stored entry is not JSON (edited by hand, written by something else), `migrate(old, fromVersion)` threw, or the storage refused the write (the quota is full, storage is blocked in a private window or by the browser's settings). The app keeps running: after a failed restore it starts from `initialState`, and after a failed write the change is simply not saved (the next change tries again). It is a warning printed in production too, since a full or blocked storage only shows up on users' machines.
Fix: For a restore failure, check the stored entry under the persist key (DevTools > Application > Local Storage) and `migrate()` for that stored version; a corrupt entry is replaced on the next save. For a write failure, save less (`pick` only what must survive a reload) or catch quota errors in a custom `storage` adapter.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG642

## SYG643

SYG643 (warn): Declaration static with no driver to take it
A component declares `timers`, `connections`, `resources` or `browser`, but no registered driver takes that static, so nothing happens and nothing else says so: the timers never fire, the connections never open, the resources stay idle, the browser sources never start. The core sends each of these statics to the source of the driver that asks for it (`makeTimerDriver()`, `makeSocketDriver()`, `makeFetchDriver()`, `makeBrowserDriver()`), and the driver is opt-in: `run()` doesn't register it for you.
Fix: Register the driver when you start the app: `run(App, { TIMER: makeTimerDriver() })` for `timers`, `run(App, { WS: makeSocketDriver() })` for `connections`, `run(App, { HTTP: makeFetchDriver() })` for `resources`, `run(App, { BROWSER: makeBrowserDriver() })` for `browser` (the key is yours to choose; the core finds the driver by the static it takes).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG643

## SYG644

SYG644 (warn): Custom element prop hides an HTMLElement member
A `defineElement(tag, Component, { props })` declaration names a prop that is also a member of `HTMLElement`, such as `title`, `hidden`, `lang`, `dir` or `translate`. The element defines its own property for each prop, so the native member of that name stops working on this element: setting `el.hidden = true` updates the prop instead of hiding the element, and the matching attribute no longer has its native effect. `sygnal/element` reports it once per tag when the element first connects, through the diagnostics core when diagnostics are on (a console warning in dev otherwise).
Fix: Rename the prop (`heading` instead of `title`, `collapsed` instead of `hidden`) and update the attribute and the component's state key that it feeds. Keep the name only when replacing the native behaviour is what you want.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG644

## SYG645

SYG645 (warn): viewTransitions that can't run
A component declares `viewTransitions` (for example `Board.viewTransitions = ['MOVE']`), but the app's DOM driver can't run View Transitions, so those actions patch the page at once, without the animation, and nothing else says so. The static only asks: the transition is run by the DOM driver from `makeViewTransitionDOMDriver()`, which is opt-in so that apps without View Transitions don't ship it, and `run()`'s default DOM driver is the plain one. Reported once per component when it starts. Not reported under `renderComponent` (the mock DOM and the `dom: 'real'` container don't animate).
Fix: Give `run()` the View Transition DOM driver: `run(App, { DOM: makeViewTransitionDOMDriver('#root') })` with `import { makeViewTransitionDOMDriver } from 'sygnal'` (use the same mount point as before). Or remove the `viewTransitions` static. For a value that isn't an array, list the action names in one: `Board.viewTransitions = ['MOVE']`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG645

## SYG660

SYG660 (error): Widget mount threw
A widget's `mount(el, props, dispatch)` threw when its host entered the page (or on the first client patch after server rendering). The widget is not mounted. The error goes to the app's `onError` hook with phase `'widget'`, and the component that renders the widget shows its `onError` fallback in the widget's place on its next render (an empty error `<div>` without one); the rest of its view keeps working. Without the dev entry it is logged as `[Sygnal SYG660]` followed by the error.
Fix: Fix `mount()` (a missing library import, an option the library rejects, a prop that is `undefined` on the first render). Give the component that renders the widget an `.onError` to show a custom fallback.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG660

## SYG661

SYG661 (error): Widget update threw or reported an error
A widget failed after it mounted: either its `update(instance, props, el)` threw when the props it was rendered with changed (a widget without `update` is remounted instead, so its `mount()` threw), or the widget reported an error itself through `error(e)`, `mount`'s fourth parameter (a failure in its own timer, callback or redraw, such as a `fromZag` render on a machine-driven update). The dev message says which: `update() threw` or `reported an error through error(e)`. Either way, as for SYG660, the error goes to the app's `onError` hook with phase `'widget'` and the owner's `onError` fallback replaces the widget on its next render.
Fix: For a throwing `update`: fix `update()` for every value the view can pass (`null`, an empty list, a value of another type). `update` gets the newest props each time they change (a shallow compare), so it should not keep the props it was first given. For `error(e)`: fix what the widget reports (the error's stack points to its timer or callback), or give the owner an `.onError` for a custom fallback.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG661

## SYG662

SYG662 (error): Widget unmount threw
A widget's `unmount(instance, el)` threw when its host left the page. The host is removed anyway, but what `unmount` didn't finish (listeners on `document`, timers, observers) may keep running. The error goes to the app's `onError` hook with phase `'widget'`; there is no fallback to show, since the widget is gone. Without the dev entry it is logged as `[Sygnal SYG662]` followed by the error.
Fix: Fix `unmount()`, for example by guarding a library's `destroy()` that throws when called twice or after its element was removed.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG662

## SYG663

SYG663 (error): Invalid browser-source spec or command
An entry of a component's `browser` static can't be started, or a command sent to the browser driver's sink can't be run, so it is skipped and nothing would happen. A `browser` entry is an object with one key that names its source (`intersection`, `resize`, `media`, `storage`, `visibility`, `online`, `geolocation`) and that names the action its events are delivered as (`action: 'SEEN'`, a string); `intersection` and `resize` take a selector in the component's own view, or `true` for its root element; a `resize` entry's `box`, when given, is `'content-box'`, `'border-box'` or `'device-pixel-content-box'`.
Fix: Write the entry as `seen: { intersection: '.cover', action: 'SEEN' }`, `dark: { media: '(prefers-color-scheme: dark)', action: 'DARK' }` (a falsy value stops it: `seen: !state.seen && { ... }`), and a command as `COPY: { BROWSER: (state) => ({ copy: state.link, ok: 'COPIED' }) }`. Clipboard reads and writes are commands, not `browser` entries.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG663

## SYG664

SYG664 (error): Browser source not in the driver
A `browser` entry (or a BROWSER command) uses a source that the app's browser driver wasn't made with: `makeBrowserDriverWith(intersectionSource, mediaSource)` takes only the sources it is given, so that the others add no bytes, and an entry of any other kind is not started. `makeBrowserDriver()` has every source.
Fix: Add the source to the driver, e.g. `makeBrowserDriverWith(intersectionSource, mediaSource, storageSource)`, or use `makeBrowserDriver()`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG664

## SYG665

SYG665 (warn): Browser source failed with no error action
A browser source or command failed: the user denied the geolocation or clipboard permission, the API isn't available (no `navigator.clipboard` outside a secure context, no `navigator.geolocation`), the position timed out, or storage is blocked or full. Its spec names no `error` action, so the component never hears about it and keeps waiting. Reported once per component, entry and kind of failure.
Fix: Name an `error` action and handle it: `here: { geolocation: true, action: 'POS', error: 'GEO_FAILED' }` with `GEO_FAILED: (state, { code, message }) => ...`, or `COPY: { BROWSER: (state) => ({ copy: state.link, ok: 'COPIED', error: 'COPY_FAILED' }) }` with `COPY_FAILED: (state, { name, message }) => ...`. Ask for permission-gated sources from a user action, and say why.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG665

## SYG666

SYG666 (error): Adapter peer dependency missing
A module imports one of Sygnal's adapter entries, but a package that entry needs isn't installed. The adapters keep their libraries as optional peer dependencies, so an app that doesn't use them never installs them: `sygnal/react` needs `react` and `react-dom` (or a `preact/compat` alias), `sygnal/zag` needs `@zag-js/vanilla`, and `sygnal/ui/menu`, `sygnal/ui/select` and `sygnal/ui/combobox` each need `@zag-js/vanilla` and their own machine (`@zag-js/menu`, `@zag-js/select`, `@zag-js/combobox`).
Fix: Install what the message lists: `npm install react react-dom` for `sygnal/react`; `npm install @zag-js/vanilla@1.45 @zag-js/menu@1.45` for `sygnal/ui/menu` (likewise `@zag-js/select` for `sygnal/ui/select`, `@zag-js/combobox` for `sygnal/ui/combobox`) (the Zag packages must share one version). For Preact, alias `react`, `react-dom` and `react-dom/client` to `preact/compat` (and `preact/compat/client`) in the bundler config.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG666

## SYG667

SYG667 (error): Invalid adapter argument
`fromZag(zag, render, options)` got a first argument that isn't a Zag machine package (an object with `machine` and `connect`, as `import * as menu from '@zag-js/menu'` gives), or a `render` that isn't a function; or `fromReact(Component, options)` got something that isn't a React component (a function, or an object such as `memo()` or `forwardRef()` returns). It is thrown when the widget is defined, at module load, so the app doesn't start with a widget that can't mount.
Fix: Pass the whole machine package and a render function: `fromZag(menu, (api, props) => <div>...</div>, { events: { select: ['onSelect', (d) => d.value] } })` with `import * as menu from '@zag-js/menu'` (not the default import or `menu.machine`). For React, pass the component itself: `fromReact(StarRating, { events: { rate: 'onChange' } })`, not an element (`<StarRating />`) or a tag name.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG667

## SYG668

SYG668 (warn): Browser source has no element to observe
An `intersection` or `resize` entry of a component's `browser` declaration has nothing to observe, so its action never comes. Either no DOM source reached the browser driver for the instance (the app runs without a DOM driver, or the declaration was sent from outside a component's `browser` static), or, under `renderComponent(C, { dom: 'real' })`, the entry's selector matches no element the component renders (a typo, or an element rendered only later). The `t.browser` fake still sends its initial report, so the test can pass while the real app observes nothing. Reported once per component, entry and reason.
Fix: Run the app with a DOM driver (`run(App, drivers, { mountPoint })`) and declare the entry in the component's own `browser` static. Use a selector the component's own view renders, or `true` for its root element: `cover: { intersection: '.cover', action: 'SEEN' }` with `<img className="cover" />` in the view. Declare the entry only while its element exists: `chart: state.open && { resize: '.chart', action: 'SIZE' }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG668

## SYG669

SYG669 (warn): Sygnal component inside a fromZag render
A `fromZag(zag, render)` widget's `render` returned a Sygnal component (`<Badge />`), a widget tag (`<Icon />`, `<Menu />`), or special JSX (`<Transition>`, `<Portal>`, `<Collection>`, `<Switchable>`, `<Suspense>`, `<ClientOnly>`, `<VirtualCollection>`, `<Slot>`, with or without props). The adapter patches its render into the widget host with a snabbdom patch of its own, outside the component tree, so none of these run there: a component isn't instantiated, a widget doesn't mount, and a marker renders as an unknown element. Only plain elements (with Zag's prop getters spread on them) work inside the render. Reported once per widget.
Fix: Render plain elements in the `render` function (`<span className="badge">{props.text}</span>` instead of `<Badge text={props.text} />`). Pass data in through the widget's props, and put components, widgets and special JSX around the widget tag in the component's view instead of inside it.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG669

## SYG670

SYG670 (error): Auth header sent from the browser to a hosted endpoint
A `sygnal/ai` HTTP transport (`openResponses`, `chatCompletions`, `anthropicMessages`, `uiMessageStream`, `agui`) running in a browser was about to send an auth header (`Authorization`, `x-api-key`, `api-key`, `x-goog-api-key`) to a host that is neither local (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, `*.localhost`) nor the page's own origin. A key in browser code ships to everyone who opens the page, who can then spend it. The request is refused before anything is sent: the chat request fails (its `error` action gets the error, or SYG678 logs it) and this message is logged, in production too.
Fix: Call the provider from your server and point the transport at that route: an AI SDK route with `uiMessageStream('/api/chat')`, or your own proxy with `openResponses({ baseURL: '/api/llm' })`, so the key stays there. Only for a key the user typed in themselves (a bring-your-own-key tool), pass `dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true` to the transport.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG670

## SYG672

SYG672 (error): Strict mode without the strict layer
A transport (`openResponses`, `chatCompletions`, `anthropicMessages`) was given `strict: true`. Strict mode rewrites every tool schema (and the `output` schema) into the provider's strict subset, and that code is imported separately, as `strictSchemas` from `sygnal/ai`, so apps that don't use strict mode don't carry it (about 1.1 KB gzipped). `strict` takes that import, not a boolean. The transport sends its requests non-strict: the model may produce arguments outside the schemas, and the agent layer and the chat driver still validate every call. Reported in development, once per transport.
Fix: Import the strict layer and pass it: `import { openResponses, strictSchemas } from 'sygnal/ai'` and `openResponses({ baseURL, model, strict: strictSchemas })`. Or drop `strict` to send portable schemas.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG672

## SYG673

SYG673 (warn): Malformed chat stream event
A chat transport (the `transport` of `makeChatDriver()`, from `sygnal/ai` or your own) yielded an event the driver can't use: not an object with a string `type`, a `text` or `reasoning` event whose `delta` isn't a string, a `tool-call` with no tool `name`, or a `tool-result` / `tool-error` whose `id` matches no tool call of the reply. The event is skipped and the stream goes on, so the reply may miss text or a tool call. Events of an unknown type are ignored silently, as the Open Responses spec requires; this is only for known types with the wrong shape. Reported for the first five such events per driver, in development.
Fix: Fix the transport so it yields `ChatEvent`s (see `sygnal/ai`): `{ type: 'text', delta: 'Hi' }`, `{ type: 'reasoning', delta }`, `{ type: 'tool-call', id, name, input }`, `{ type: 'tool-result', id, output }`, `{ type: 'data', name, data }`, `{ type: 'finish', reason, usage }`. A transport that parses a wire format should map each provider event to one of these and drop the ones it doesn't know.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG673

## SYG674

SYG674 (info): WebMCP not available
`experimentalExposeWebMcp()` found no WebMCP context: no `modelContext` option, and neither `document.modelContext` nor the older `navigator.modelContext` exists. That is the normal case in browsers without WebMCP (Chrome before the origin trial, Firefox, Safari) and on insecure pages, so it is only information: the call does nothing and returns a `stop()` whose `available` is `false`. Chrome 153 exposes WebMCP behind `chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing` (`--enable-features=WebMCP`) or an origin trial token.
Fix: Nothing to fix. To try it elsewhere, install `@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill` (`installWebMCP()`) before the call, or pass `modelContext`. Use `stop.available` to show or hide UI that depends on an agent.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG674

## SYG675

SYG675 (info): Tool sent non-strict under strict mode
A transport with `strict: strictSchemas` (`openResponses`, `chatCompletions`, `anthropicMessages`) rewrites each tool's input schema (and the `output` schema) into the provider's strict subset, so the model can only produce arguments that match. A schema with no strict form, such as a record (`z.record()`, `additionalProperties` with a schema) or a non-object root, and for Anthropic also a recursive schema, a value of any type, or a schema past Anthropic's per-request limits (20 strict tools, 24 optional and 16 union-typed parameters across the strict schemas), is sent non-strict on its own while the other tools stay strict.
Fix: Give the schema a strict form: an object root with named properties instead of a record (for example an array of `{ key, value }` objects). Or accept the non-strict tool: validation still protects the state.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG675

## SYG676

SYG676 (warn): WebMCP registerTool rejected
`experimentalExposeWebMcp()` registers each agent tool with `document.modelContext.registerTool()`, which returns a Promise. The browser refused one: most often `InvalidStateError: Duplicate tool name` (another script, a second `experimentalExposeWebMcp()` call on the same page, or a declarative form registered the same name first), or an invalid name or empty description. The rejection is reported, never thrown, and that tool stays unavailable to the agent until its name, description or schema changes. Reported once per tool and registration, in development.
Fix: Give each exposure its own `prefix` (`experimentalExposeWebMcp(app, { prefix: 'shop_' })`), rename the clashing `agent` declaration or form `toolname`, and call `stop()` before exposing the same app again.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG676

## SYG677

SYG677 (warn): Chat request sent from outside a component
A request reached `makeChatDriver()` without the sender stamp the core puts on every value a component's model sends. The chat driver answers only with reply actions (`delta`, `tool`, `ok`, `error`) on the component that sent the request, and it has no `select()` stream, so a request from anywhere else (a stream written into the driver's sink by hand, a driver wrapper that rebuilds the request object, a test that calls the driver directly) could never be answered. It is dropped, and nothing is streamed.
Fix: Send chat requests from a component's model: `SEND: { LLM: (state) => ({ messages: state.messages, delta: 'DELTA', ok: 'DONE', error: 'FAILED' }) }`. A wrapper around the driver must pass the request object through unchanged (or copy its non-enumerable sender stamp). In tests, use `renderComponent`'s LLM fake (`t.stream('LLM', chunks)`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG677

## SYG678

SYG678 (error): Chat request failed with no error action
A `makeChatDriver()` request failed (the network or the provider returned an error, the transport threw, or the structured `output` was not valid JSON or failed its schema), and the request names no `error` action. The chat driver has no `errors()` stream, so without an `error` action the component never hears of the failure and stays in its streaming state. The driver logs the failure with this code, in production too. A stream that was aborted (`abort`, `latest`, a removed component, the app disposed) is not a failure and is never reported.
Fix: Name an `error` action on the request and handle it: `{ messages, delta: 'DELTA', ok: 'DONE', error: 'FAILED' }` with `FAILED: (state, { error, issues }) => ({ ...state, status: 'error', error: error.message })`. In tests, `t.fail('LLM', error)` drives that action.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG678

## SYG679

SYG679 (error): Invalid chat request
A value sent to a `makeChatDriver()` sink is not a request the driver can send: it isn't an object, it has no `messages` array, its `coalesce` is not `'frame'`, `'none'` or a number of milliseconds, or its `output` is not a Standard Schema (an object with `~standard.validate`). The request is not sent, so no reply action follows. Stopping a stream is `{ abort: key }` or `{ abort: true }`, not a request.
Fix: Send `{ messages: [...], ok: 'DONE', error: 'FAILED' }` (add `delta: 'DELTA'` to stream, `key` to name the request, `output: schema` for structured output with a Zod, Valibot or ArkType schema), or `{ abort: 'reply' }` to stop one. Return `ABORT` (or nothing) from the model entry when there is nothing to send.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG679

## SYG680

SYG680 (info): Part is LLM-only under a decision backend
A catalog part has a free-text param (`type: 'text'` or `type: 'list'`) that is `required` and has no `default`. A decision model (`compose.decisions()`: TypeSafe Jev, Ollama `nimble`) only chooses among options the app declared; it never writes text, so it can't fill that param. `compose.decisions()` leaves the part out of its questions and never places it: the part is LLM-only. `compose.llm()` still uses it. Free-text params that have a `default` are fine: a decision model keeps the default. Collected once per part (info).
Fix: Nothing to fix if the part is meant for LLM backends only. To let a decision model place it, give the param a `default` (`{ type: 'text', default: 'Notes' }`), or turn it into choices: `options: { value: description }` (an enum) or a number with `bins`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG680

## SYG681

SYG681 (error): Compose backend option problem
The `compose` behavior (sygnal/ai) needs a backend, `compose.decisions({ model, … })` or `compose.llm({ model, … })`, and a catalog made by `defineCatalog()`: without them `compose()` throws with this code. `compose.decisions()` made without a `model` is reported in development: its `decide()` requests name no model, which a decision service rejects unless your server route fills it in. `compose.llm()` without a `model` is not reported: the chat transport sends its own default (`openResponses({ model })`, …).
Fix: Pass both: `compose(catalog, { backend: compose.decisions({ model: 'jev-latest' }) })`. For `compose.decisions()`, pass the model even when your server picks one, so the request documents it.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG681

## SYG682

SYG682 (warn): Decision model answered outside the criteria
A reply to a `compose.decisions()` step answered a choice question with a value that is not one of the question's options (its `criteria`), for example a part id the request never offered or a mistyped option in a proxy or fixture. `compose.decisions()` rebuilds each step's questions from the pending state and checks every answer against them; the bad answer is ignored, as if the question had no answer (a part isn't used, a param keeps its default, a place falls back to the part's first allowed place), and the composition continues.
Fix: Check what answers the decision endpoint: a server route that rewrites replies, a model that ignores the criteria, or a test reply written by hand. In tests, build replies with `answers(questions, picks)` (it rejects unknown options) or `composeWith`. If a model keeps answering outside the criteria, report it with the request's questions.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG682

## SYG683

SYG683 (error): LLM layout invalid after repair
`compose.llm()` asks the model for a layout tree with structured output: a JSON Schema built from the catalog (one closed object per part, enum params, record values from state, rows holding parts only, `maxDepth`). Most providers enforce the schema while decoding, but some don't (no strict mode, an unconstrained local model), and a schema can't say everything, so every reply is read leniently (`type` or `name` for `part`, flat params, the list under another key) and repaired: unknown parts dropped, a part used more than its `maxUses`, a bad param value replaced by its default, text cut to its `maxLength`, a row of one unwrapped.
Fix: Send the request through a transport that enforces structured output (`openResponses` or `chatCompletions` with `strict: strictSchemas`, Ollama's `format`), lower the temperature, or use a model that follows JSON Schemas. Check that the part ids in the catalog's `examples` exist. The diagnostic's `data` holds the reply and the issues found.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG683

## SYG684

SYG684 (warn): Client tool shadows an agent tool
`chat({ clientTools })` (sygnal/ai) declares tools the app answers itself: their calls stay open (`input-available`) until `'assistant.TOOL_OUTPUT'` answers them, or, for the `ask_user` tool of `chat({ ask })`, until a card's result part answers. Here a client tool has the same name as a tool the agent layer made from an `agent` declaration (`<name>_<action>`), so a request can't send both. The client tool is sent and its calls are the app's to answer; the agent action is not offered to the model. Reported once per name, in development.
Fix: Rename the client tool (`clientTools: { pick_date: … }`), or the agent declaration's `name` or the action, so each tool name is unique. `ask_user` is taken when `chat({ ask })` is used.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG684

## SYG685

SYG685 (warn): Answer for a tool call that is not open
`'assistant.TOOL_OUTPUT'` (`{ toolCallId, output }` or `{ toolCallId, errorText }`) or a card's answer (`ANSWER`, from a result part's `compose.answer(props, value)`) arrived for a call that is not waiting for one. Only a client tool call that is still `input-available` in the last assistant message can be answered (an `ask_user` card only while it is open). The call may have been answered already, closed by STOP or by a new message ("not answered: …"), dropped with its message by REGENERATE, or it may be an agent tool call, which the agent layer runs.
Fix: Answer only the calls in `openToolCalls(state.assistant)`, with the part's `toolCallId`. Disable the answer controls when the call is no longer open (an answered card renders frozen with `askCard`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG685

## SYG686

SYG686 (warn): Ask catalog without a result part
`chat({ ask: { catalog } })` (sygnal/ai) gives the model the `ask_user` tool: a card is composed from the catalog's parts, and the call waits until a result part (`result: true`) answers it with `compose.answer(props, value)`. This catalog has no part with `result: true`, so no card it can build is answerable: every `ask_user` call stays open until the user presses Stop or sends a new message. Reported once per `chat()` call, also in production.
Fix: Mark the parts the user answers with `result: true` (a choice, a picker, a form, a yes/no) and send `compose.answer(props, value)` to PARENT from their model, for example `PICK: { PARENT: (_s, value, _n, props) => compose.answer(props, value) }`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG686

## SYG687

SYG687 (warn): LLM reply stopped in a loop or cut short
`compose.llm()` stopped reading the model's reply before it ended, and used what came before the stop. A small model asked for a change it can't express (before edits had `wrap`, qwen3:8b met "put the dates and amount in a Trip section" with `add dates top, add amount top, …`) can repeat the same operations without end; every list in the reply's JSON Schema has a `maxItems`, but not every provider enforces it.
Fix: Check what the change asked for and what the reply did (`decisions.ops`); rephrasing the change, or sending it as a fresh composition (`{ prompt, fresh: true }`), often helps a small model. Use a transport and model that enforce the schema (Ollama's structured output does, `strict: strictSchemas` on OpenAI), or raise `maxTokens` if a long page was cut. The diagnostic's `data` holds the reply.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG687

## SYG690

SYG690 (warn): API contract skew
`contractFetch()` (sygnal/api) wraps the `fetch` of `makeFetchDriver` and `makeSocketDriver` and watches for the answer `contractSkew()` gives on the server: a 409 `CONTRACT_SKEW` with an `x-contract-skew` header. It means the app sends a contract hash (`contractHash(contract)` in a header, through the client's `headers` option) that differs from the server's: the tab was loaded before a deploy changed the API, so its requests may no longer match the server's inputs or outputs. Each such request fails with `isContractSkew(failure)` true in its `error` action (a resource has `status: 'error'`).
Fix: Offer a reload from `onSkew` (`contractFetch({ onSkew: () => showReloadBanner() })`) or from the `error` action (`isContractSkew(failure)`). Deploy the client and the server together, and send the hash of the contract the client was built with.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG690

## SYG691

SYG691 (warn): Unknown API endpoint
A member chain on a client made by `orpcClient(contract)` (sygnal/api) names a procedure or router that the contract doesn't have, such as `api.quotes.lst()` for a contract with `quotes.list`. The client mirrors the contract router: each procedure is an endpoint function, each router an object, so the misspelled name is `undefined`, and calling it throws `TypeError: api.quotes.lst is not a function` when the model entry or resource runs. TypeScript reports this in a typed project; sygnal-check follows the client to its `orpcClient(...)` call and the contract to its object literal, through imports, so plain JavaScript gets it too.
Fix: Use the procedure's name as the contract declares it (the message suggests the closest one), or add the procedure to the contract and implement it on the server. For a `*.server` import, import the server function's name, and move a constant or helper the client needs into a shared module that both sides import.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG691

## SYG692

SYG692 (warn): Sandbox event dropped
A sandboxed component (`createSandbox` or `<Sandboxed>` from sygnal/sandbox) sent an `EVENTS` value the page did not accept, so it never reached `onEmit` or the tag's `emit` event. The page accepts only the types declared in `emits`, and only data that passes that type's Standard Schema (zod, valibot, arktype, ...): the guest is untrusted code, so its events are untrusted input, and the host's intent should only ever see validated data. The message says which: a type not declared in `emits` (an inherited name such as `constructor` never counts), invalid data (with the schema's issues), a schema that threw, or no `emits` at all.
Fix: Declare the type with a schema for its data, `emits={{ ANSWER: AnswerSchema }}`, or fix the guest so it sends what the schema expects. If the guest should not send that event, nothing needs fixing: dropping it is the protection.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG692

## SYG701

SYG701 (warn): Click listener on a non-interactive element
The intent listens for clicks (`DOM.click('.card')`, `DOM.select('.card').events('click')`, or a control such as `controls({ Card: 'div' })`) on an element that is not interactive, such as a `<div>`, `<span>`, `<li>`, `<p>` or `<img>`, and that has no `role` and `tabIndex`. Mouse users can click it, but keyboard users can't focus it and screen readers don't announce it as something to activate, so the action is out of their reach. sygnal-check matches the intent selector against the component's own view;
Fix: Render a `<button type="button">` (or declare the control as `'button'`) and style it as needed. If the element must stay a `<div>`, add `role="button" tabIndex={0}` and also handle `DOM.keydown(x)` for Enter and Space. To keep one on purpose, add `// sygnal-ignore SYG701` above the intent line.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG701

## SYG702

SYG702 (warn): Form field without an accessible label
An `<input>` (other than hidden, submit, reset, button or image), `<select>` or `<textarea>` has no accessible name: no `<label>` wraps it, no `<label for>` matches its id, and it has no `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `title` or `placeholder`. Screen readers then announce only "edit text" or "combo box". A `placeholder` counts as a last-resort name (as axe does), though a visible label is better. sygnal-check follows the field to the component or helper that renders it and accepts a label around every place it is used; a `uid('x')` id matches a label with the same `uid('x')` call.
Fix: Wrap the field: `<label>Email <input type="email" /></label>`, or link them by id: `<label for={uid('email')}>Email</label><input id={uid('email')} />` (`uid` is a view prop). For a field with no visible label, add `aria-label="Search"`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG702

## SYG703

SYG703 (warn): Image without alt text
An `<img>` has no `alt` attribute. Screen readers then read out the file name, or skip the image without saying what it shows. `alt=""` is allowed: it marks the image as decorative. Images named another way (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `title`) or hidden (`role="presentation"`, `aria-hidden`) are not reported. It is a warning, also under `--strict`; `--a11y=error` (or `a11y: 'error'` in `check()` and the Vite plugin's `check` options) makes it an error.
Fix: Add `alt="what the image shows"` (for a dynamic image, `alt={item.name}`); for a purely decorative image use `alt=""`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG703

## SYG704

SYG704 (warn): Link without href used as a button
The intent listens for clicks on an `<a>` that has no `href`. Without `href` an `<a>` is not focusable and is announced as plain text, so keyboard and screen-reader users can't trigger the action. sygnal-check matches the intent's click selectors against the component's own view, like SYG701. It is a warning, also under `--strict`; `--a11y=error` (or `a11y: 'error'` in `check()` and the Vite plugin's `check` options) makes it an error.
Fix: For an action, render `<button type="button">` (styled as a link if needed). For navigation, give the `<a>` a real `href` (with the router, `href={router.href('task', { id })}`).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG704

## SYG705

SYG705 (warn): Button without an accessible name
A `<button>` has no text content and no `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or `title`, so screen readers announce only "button". This is usually an icon-only button: an `<i>`, an `<svg>` without `<title>`, or an `<img alt="">`. Only literal children are checked: a button whose children include an expression (`{state.label}`), a function call or a child component is not reported.
Fix: Put text in the button, or for an icon-only button add `aria-label="Close"` and mark the icon `aria-hidden="true"`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG705

## SYG706

SYG706 (warn): Positive tabIndex
An element has `tabIndex` greater than 0. Positive values move it ahead of every element with `tabIndex={0}` or none, so the Tab order no longer follows the page, and every other positive value has to be kept in step by hand. It is a warning, also under `--strict`; `--a11y=error` (or `a11y: 'error'` in `check()` and the Vite plugin's `check` options) makes it an error.
Fix: Use `tabIndex={0}` to make an element focusable in document order, or `tabIndex={-1}` to focus it only from code. Change the order of the markup if the Tab order should change.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG706

## SYG707

SYG707 (warn): Unknown ARIA attribute or invalid role
An element has an `aria-*` attribute that is not in WAI-ARIA (usually a typo such as `aria-lable` or `aria-labeledby`), or a `role` that is not a WAI-ARIA role: a typo, or an abstract role such as `widget` or `section` that authors may not use. Assistive technology ignores both, so the intended label, state or role never reaches users. The lists are WAI-ARIA 1.2 plus the 1.3 additions, and the `doc-*` and `graphics-*` role modules; dynamic role values are not checked. It is a warning, also under `--strict`; `--a11y=error` (or `a11y: 'error'` in `check()` and the Vite plugin's `check` options) makes it an error.
Fix: Fix the spelling (the message suggests the closest name), or use a concrete role such as `button`, `checkbox`, `tab` or `region`. For your own data, use a `data-*` attribute.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG707

## SYG708

SYG708 (warn): Label or ARIA reference to an id that is not rendered
A `<label for>`, `aria-describedby` or `aria-labelledby` names an id that no element renders, so the label or description is attached to nothing (often a typo, or an id that was renamed on one side only). A literal id may be rendered anywhere in the checked files; a `uid('x')` reference needs an element in the same component with `id={uid('x')}`. When some id in the project is dynamic (`id={props.id}`), literal references are not checked, and dynamic references never are. It is a warning, also under `--strict`; `--a11y=error` (or `a11y: 'error'` in `check()` and the Vite plugin's `check` options) makes it an error.
Fix: Render the target with the same id, or fix the reference. Inside a component, use `uid('x')` on both sides: `<input id={uid('email')} aria-describedby={uid('email-error')} />` and `<p id={uid('email-error')}>`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG708

## SYG722

SYG722 (warn): Menu, Select or Combobox without an accessible name
A `<Menu>`, `<Select>` or `<Combobox>` from `sygnal/ui/menu`, `sygnal/ui/select` or `sygnal/ui/combobox` has no `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The part names its control from them (Menu's trigger text is its `label`; Select's trigger and Combobox's input are labelled by the visible `label`, or take `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` directly), so without any of them a screen reader announces an unnamed menu button or combobox. A dynamic value or a spread counts as a name; an empty string doesn't. It is a warning, also under `--strict`;
Fix: Give it a visible label: `<Select className="size" label="Size" items={SIZES} />`. When the label is elsewhere on the page, point at it with `aria-labelledby="<its id>"`; for an icon-only Menu trigger, use `aria-label="More actions"`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG722

## SYG724

SYG724 (warn): Sortable handle not keyboard-accessible, or no live region
A `sortable` use whose keyboard path or announcements can't work. Keyboard moves start on the handle (the item when there is no `handle` option): sygnal-check finds the elements that match it in the host's view and the views it renders (Collection items, children) and reports one that can't take focus (not a button, field, link with `href` or `summary`, no `tabIndex` or `tabIndex={-1}`, not contenteditable), or a focusable one other than a `<button>` (SYG705 covers those) with no `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` / `title` and no content.
Fix: Render the handle as `<button type="button" className="grip" aria-label={'Reorder ' + state.title} aria-describedby={context.sort.helpId}>`, and the message in a live region: `<p role="status" aria-live="assertive">{state.sort.message}</p>`. An app-wide announcer elsewhere: `// sygnal-ignore SYG724`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG724

## SYG730

SYG730 (warn): Action reachable only by hovering
An intent action's stream comes only from `mouseenter` / `mouseover` (or `pointerenter` / `pointerover`) listeners, nothing else triggers it (no other DOM event in that stream, no `next()`, reply action, connection, timer or behavior), and its model entry changes the state. Keyboard users never hover and touch screens hover only on a tap, so what it shows (a tooltip, a preview, a menu) or does can't be reached by them. An `agent` declaration doesn't count as a path: it serves agents, not people. Only streams the checker can see in full are judged (DOM listeners with literal event names, xstream operators, callbacks);
Fix: Trigger the action from focus too, and close it on blur and Escape as on mouse leave: `SHOW: xs.merge(DOM.mouseenter('.card'), DOM.focusin('.card'))`, `HIDE: xs.merge(DOM.mouseleave('.card'), DOM.focusout('.card'))`; give the element a way to take focus (a `<button>`). For a tooltip, `tooltip()` from `sygnal/ui` handles hover, focus and Escape (`tooltips()` for many triggers on one component, such as glossary terms).
More: sygnal-check explain SYG730

## SYG731

SYG731 (warn): Toggled state shown only by a class
An element that a click listener targets shows an on/off or selected state only through a class that follows the state (`className={{ done: state.done }}`, `className={state.filter === 'done' ? 'selected' : ''}`), while the click's own STATE reducer flips that field (`done: !state.done`) or, for an equality, writes it (`filter: 'done'`). Sighted users see the change; a screen reader announces a plain button.
Fix: For an on/off toggle (the reducer flips `!field`), expose the state with the same condition as the class: `<button className={{ done: state.done }} aria-pressed={state.done}>`; `aria-selected` for a tab or listbox option, `aria-expanded` for a disclosure, `aria-checked` with `role="switch"`, `aria-current="page"` for the current link. Or use a native `<input type="checkbox">` with a label. For a change that isn't a toggle, announce it: let the text or `aria-label` follow the same condition, or add `aria-live="polite"` / `role="status"`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG731

## SYG900

SYG900 (warn): A diagnostics check threw
A diagnostics check itself crashed: one of the `sygnal/diagnostics` runtime checks threw inside a hook, or a `sygnal-check` rule threw (or a file could not be parsed). The failure is isolated, so the app and the other checks keep running, but that check produced no results for the code involved. This points to a bug in the checker, or (for parse errors) a syntax error in your file.
Fix: For a parse error, fix the syntax error in the named file; for a config-file finding, fix or remove the named key (or the JSON syntax); otherwise please report it to Sygnal with the file or component that triggers it.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG900

## SYG901

SYG901 (error): Retired in 6.0: Sub-component sink stream errored
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was logged when the stream merging a component's sub-component sinks errored, an internal of the core Sygnal 6.0 replaced. The 6.0 core has no such stream: an error in a child's reducer, view or driver value is reported under that phase's own code (SYG216, SYG406, ...) and the app's `onError` hook.
Fix: Nothing to change: errors are reported under their phase's own code (SYG216, SYG406, ...) and the app's `onError` hook.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG901

## SYG902

SYG902 (error): Retired in 6.0: EFFECT stream errored
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was logged when the stream running a component's EFFECT entries errored, an internal of the core Sygnal 6.0 replaced. In 6.0 an EFFECT runs synchronously with its action; a throwing EFFECT is reported as SYG216 (with the `onError` hook) and later actions keep running.
Fix: Nothing to change: a throwing EFFECT is reported as SYG216 and the app's `onError` hook, and later actions keep running.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG902

## SYG903

SYG903 (error): Retired in 6.0: Component factory returned invalid sinks
Retired in 6.0 and never reported. It was thrown when a component factory (the removed `component()` / `collection()` / `switchable()` helpers, or a hand-written one) returned something other than a sinks object. Sygnal 6.0 instantiates every component from its function; there are no factories.
Fix: Nothing to change. Pass component functions to JSX, `of` and `CHILD.select`.
More: sygnal-check explain SYG903

## SandboxLimits

SandboxLimits (interface, sygnal/sandbox)
export interface SandboxLimits
Members:
  memoryBytes: number - QuickJS's heap (default 32 MB)
  stackBytes: number - QuickJS's stack (default 256 KB; at most 384 KB: above that a recursion can crash the WASM module)
  maxWasmBytes: number - the instance's whole linear memory, ArrayBuffers included (default 64 MB)
  bootMs: number - kernel + component + first render (default 1000 ms)
  callMs: number - one event, timer or fetch reply with its render (default 100 ms; polled, see the guide)
  cpuShare: number - guest time per rolling second (default 0.5)
  hardMs: number - worker: terminated when it doesn't answer the watchdog this long (default 1000 ms)
  maxTimers: number - pending timers (default 64)
  minTimerMs: number - the shortest timer (default 4 ms)
  maxFetches: number - fetches in flight (default 4)
  maxMessageBytes: number - one render or response (default 1 MB)
  maxLogs: number - console lines (default 100)

## SygnalPluginOptions.api

SygnalPluginOptions.api?: { handler?: string; prefix?: string; contracts?: string[]; functions?: boolean | { dir?: string; header?: string;}; }
sygnal/api (experimental): wire the app's API into the dev server and the client build. - `handler`: a module whose default export is a Fetch handler (Request → Response), served in dev at `prefix` (default '/api'); a production server mounts the same module. - `contracts`: contract modules (oRPC) that client code gets as routes and a build-time contractHash only, without their schemas (not under Vitest; leave a module out to validate replies on the client). - `functions`: function-first `*.server.ts` files under `dir` (default 'src'): replaced in client code by stubs that build the requests; `header` (default 'x-api-functions') carries each file's contract hash.
Example: const api = orpcClient(contract, { prefix: '/api' })
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/typed-apis.md

## SygnalPluginOptions.check

SygnalPluginOptions.check?: boolean | CheckPluginOptions
Run sygnal-check (an optional dependency) in dev on startup and after every source change. Findings go to the terminal and the browser console; error-severity findings also to Vite's error overlay. Skipped silently when sygnal-check isn't installed.
Example: sygnal({ diagnostics: { mode: 'error', strict: true }, check: { strict: true } })
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/forms.md

## SygnalPluginOptions.compile

SygnalPluginOptions.compile?: boolean | { views?: boolean; ssr?: boolean; blocks?: boolean; test?: boolean; }
Experimental: compile JSX views at build time. Vite 8 only (a no-op with a warning below); files under node_modules are never compiled. `true`: every part that has shipped; an object turns parts off (each defaults to true): - `views`: an HTML element (not a form field, custom element or SVG tag) becomes a direct vnode call, its data made once at module load when its attributes are static. The vnodes are the ones the JSX runtime makes. - `ssr`: in server builds, compiled elements render to HTML strings inside renderToString (the same HTML, no vnode per element). Never under Vitest.
Example: sygnal({ compile: true })
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/api-facts.md

## SygnalPluginOptions.devtools

SygnalPluginOptions.devtools?: boolean | { redux?: boolean; }
In dev (`vite`, never `vite build` or Vitest), import 'sygnal/devtools' in the same files as the diagnostics snippet. It installs the DevTools bridge (`window.__SYGNAL_DEVTOOLS__`) for the browser extension. Production builds never contain it. false: not injected. `{ redux: true }` also sends the actions and the root's state to the Redux DevTools extension (connectReduxDevtools() from 'sygnal/devtools').
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/diagnostics.md

## SygnalPluginOptions.diagnostics

SygnalPluginOptions.diagnostics?: DiagnosticsPluginOptions | DiagnosticsMode
Runtime diagnostics in dev (`vite`, never `vite build`). In every file that imports `run` from 'sygnal' the plugin sets the dev flag and imports 'sygnal/diagnostics' (the runtime checks); the Vike and Astro client entries get the same. 'off' injects none of it (DevTools: see `devtools`). Any other mode than 'warn', or an ignore list, is passed as run()'s `diagnostics` option, unless the run() call sets that option itself.
Example: run(App, drivers, { diagnostics: 'warn' })
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/diagnostics.md

## SygnalPluginOptions.disableHmr

SygnalPluginOptions.disableHmr?: boolean
Disable automatic HMR wiring.

## SygnalPluginOptions.disableJsx

SygnalPluginOptions.disableJsx?: boolean
Disable automatic JSX configuration.

## SygnalPluginOptions.graph

SygnalPluginOptions.graph?: boolean
Serve the live app graph page at `/__sygnal/graph` on the dev server (requests from this machine with a local Host / Origin only, as `/__sygnal/mcp`), built by sygnal-check and updated on every save; its URL is printed under Vite's. Skipped silently when sygnal-check isn't installed. In dev the component functions also get their static key (non-enumerable, read by inspect() as `key`), and with DevTools on the open app tabs answer the page's "Live data" (mounted components, instance counts, action flashes, state). Dev server only: production builds contain none of it.
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/diagnostics.md

## SygnalPluginOptions.mcp

SygnalPluginOptions.mcp?: boolean | McpPluginOptions
Serve an MCP endpoint at `/__sygnal/mcp` on the dev server (streamable HTTP; requests from this machine with a local Host / Origin only), so a coding agent can read and drive the running apps in the open page: get_state, dispatch, component_tree, recent_actions, get_diagnostics, copy_as_test, agent_tools, apps, tabs, and sygnal-check's check / graph / explain when it is installed. Every run() app of the page is served (`app` picks one). MCP revisions 2026-07-28 (stateless) and 2024-11-05 … 2025-11-25 (initialize); answers are application/json (no SSE stream, no sessions). Dev server only; it also loads 'sygnal/devtools' in the page.
Read: node_modules/sygnal/dist/guide/mcp-apps.md

## SygnalPluginOptions.nativeGlobalThis

SygnalPluginOptions.nativeGlobalThis?: boolean
Resolve xstream's `globalthis` dependency to a tiny stub that returns the native `globalThis`, instead of the npm polyfill and its dependency chain (~4 KB gzip), in dev, build and Vitest (a `resolve.alias`; every dependency's `globalthis` import gets the stub). Not added when your own `resolve.alias` already maps `globalthis`. false: keep the original package.

## SygnalPluginOptions.productionMessages

SygnalPluginOptions.productionMessages?: "full" | "short"
In `vite build` client code, Sygnal's own messages are reduced to the code, the component name and the docs URL, and per-component debug logging (`Component.debug`, `SYGNAL_DEBUG`) is removed. 'full': keep the complete messages and the logging.

## SygnalPluginOptions.vitestSetup

SygnalPluginOptions.vitestSetup?: boolean
Under Vitest, add the 'sygnal/diagnostics' entry to `test.setupFiles` so tests (e.g. renderComponent) get the runtime checks.

## TIMER

TIMER (driver sink and source, from makeTimerDriver)
runs the components' `timers` statics: `run(App, { TIMER: makeTimerDriver() })`. The key is free (the core finds the driver by the static it takes); `TIMER` by convention. Each timer's action goes to the instance that declared it. A disposed instance's timers stop; app dispose stops them all.
Example: run(App, { TIMER: makeTimerDriver() })
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/commands.md

## WidgetDefinition.children

WidgetDefinition.children?: true | "hidden"
Declarative children (an "island": a WebGL scene's objects, a map's markers, a chart's series). The tag's JSX children are rendered by the app's DOM driver into a container in the host (`[data-widget-children]`), as ordinary elements: components, `<Collection>`, isolation and intents work inside. `sync` gets them; the widget paints them its own way and dispatches DOM events on them. `true`: the container is visually hidden but in the accessibility tree (Enter / Space on a focused child is its `click`; `focus` is told); `'hidden'`: hidden from everything.

## form.dynamic

## form.request

the form sends a valid submit itself on the `http` sink: a request, or a function of the schema's output and the host's state (`(data, state) => ({ url: '/api/items/' + state.id, method: 'PUT' })`; `ABORT` / falsy sends nothing and leaves the submit pending). The form adds the body (`multipart: data` when a top-level value is a File or files, else `json: data`, unless the request sets `json`, `multipart` or `body`), `progress: 'form.PROGRESS'` for a multipart submit or `progress: true` (a JSON submit stays on fetch: progress goes over XMLHttpRequest) and its own `ok: 'form.DONE'`, `error: 'form.ERRORS'`

## pager

pager (function, sygnal)
A page cursor (GS-1): `List.uses = { pager: pager({ pageSize: 10, total, next: Newer, prev: Older }) }` gives `state.pager = { page, pageSize, total, offset, pages, hasPrev, hasNext }` and the actions 'pager.NEXT' / 'pager.PREV' (no change at the bounds), 'pager.GOTO' (a page number, clamped) and 'pager.SET_TOTAL' (the item count).

  page?: number - Starting page, from 0 (default 0)

  steps: { [K in keyof NoInfer<LOCAL>]: WizardStep<DRAFT, NoInfer<LOCAL>… - The steps, in order: name -> definition
  draft?: DRAFT | ((state: HOST, bag: BehaviorBag<HOST>) => DRAFT) - The draft a flow starts with, or a function of the host's state called at each start
  draftKey?: DK - The draft's key in a step's state (default 'draft');
  key?: (state: HOST, bag: BehaviorBag<HOST>) => any - The flow key (a record, session or report id). Only a change from one key to another starts the flow over;
  next?: BehaviorTarget - Selectors (or controls) whose clicks move: NEXT, BACK, RESET, GOTO (a `data-step` attribute names the step)
  back?: BehaviorTarget
  reset?: BehaviorTarget
  goto?: BehaviorTarget
  finish?: string - A host action dispatched (with the draft) by NEXT on the last step, or a step's `{ wizard: 'FINISH' }`
  dirty?: (step: any, name: keyof LOCAL & string, bag: BehaviorBag<HOST>)… - The leave guard (a step's own `dirty` wins): while true, navigating away from the flow is held for a confirm
  also: discard, groups, dialog, resetTo, restart, confirm, leave, stay, url, router
Example: wizard<Draft, State, { review: ReviewState }>
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/ui.md

## wizard.dirty

wizard.dirty?: (step: any, name: keyof LOCAL & string, bag: BehaviorBag<HOST>) => boolean
The leave guard (a step's own `dirty` wins): while true, navigating away from the flow is held for a confirm
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/ui.md

## wizard.groups

wizard.groups?: Record<string, { label?: string | ((step: any, bag: BehaviorBag<HOST>) => string); }>
Group labels: `{ build: { label } }` (default: the label of the step that applies)
Example: groups: { build: { label } }
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/ui.md

## wizard.resetTo

wizard.resetTo?: RouterCommand<Record<string, string>> | ((wizard: WizardState<DRAFT, LOCAL>, bag: BehaviorBag<HOST>) => RouterCommand<Record<string, string>>)
Where Start over navigates (a router command, or a function of the slice being reset and the bag); url mode default: the first step's route
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/ui.md

## wizard.url

wizard.url?: { route: string; param: string; key?: string; from?: (state: HOST, bag: BehaviorBag<HOST>) => Route<string>; }
The step (and the flow key) in the URL: route `route`'s param `param` names the step, query `key` the flow key; `from` maps the host's route (and an attempted one) onto it
Example: { url: '/items/2' }
Read: node_modules/sygnal/llms/ui.md
